## [4.689.41] - 2026-09-03

### Fixed

- **Scan folders added from Settings could all fail on Windows.** Explorer's
  "Copy as path" wraps the path in quotes, and pasting that stored them
  verbatim -- the folder could not be opened and the scanner ran with **no
  roots at all, silently**. Quotes are now stripped both when a path is entered
  and when one is read back, so a configuration that already has them recovers
  without being retyped.
- **Only the first PDF thumbnail was ever rendered** after the server started;
  every later one wrote a placeholder into the cache permanently.
- **With two config files present, the Python and Rust builds could not see
  each other's extension settings.** `config.toml` now takes precedence and is
  written back in the format it was read.
- **`--host` / `--port` / `--db` in `launch-args.txt` lost to the config file
  and were silently ignored.** An unrecognised flag there also fell back to the
  Python build without saying why.
- **Registered scan folders could disappear from the screen**, and added or
  removed files were not always picked up.
- **Statistics (`/api/stats/*`) recomputed from scratch on every request**,
  taking seconds.
- **Scan-folder recovery returned 400** in Settings.
- **The Bluesky integration settings never displayed the values you saved.**
- **The backup list and status reported "no backups" and "backups disabled"
  without checking.** That subsystem is not in the Rust build, so those
  endpoints now say so honestly, and the page distinguishes "none" from
  "unavailable".
- **An interrupted scan offered no way to resume.** The thumbnail cache always
  reported 0 bytes and the gateway backend list was always empty; both now read
  the real state.

### Accessibility

- **Four contrast failures fixed.** Some theme colours were never defined, so a
  dark-theme colour was used on the light background and text was hard to read.
  One of them affected 72 places.
- **Settings sidebar entries were 19.5px tall** -- under WCAG's 24px minimum
  target size.
- **Confirmation dialogs were announced as an unnamed region** by screen
  readers; they now carry a role and an accessible name.

### Fast mode

- **The download source is now a three-way choice** (auto / download / build
  locally).
- **Local build progress is shown in Settings.** It could previously appear to
  hang when its output was blocked.
- **"I enabled it and nothing happens" is fixed**, along with fast mode reading
  a different database and the source setting never being read.
- **The Hailo sidecar (`yu-infer`) was missing from the download.**

### Security

- **The raw config editor is now reachable only from the local machine.**
- **Extension sandbox profiles were written to a predictable path in a
  world-writable directory.**
- **The bridge's HTTP client could follow a `file://` URL.**
- **Reading a setting consumed the same tight rate limit as writing one**, so
  reloading your own configuration a few times could be refused.
- **LAN share imports now verify the received size against the size the peer
  declared**, so a truncated file is no longer treated as a complete one.

### Other

- The Python bundled with the portable build is now 3.13.
- Twelve page titles were never translated; they are now, and the product name
  is consistently `YU AI Manager`.

## [4.681.3] - 2026-08-29

### Fixed

- **Four LAN Cowork fixes now actually ship.** The pinned revision of the lan-cowork crate predated them, so up to v4.681.2 they took effect only on the Python path. Bumping the pin brings them into the Rust build.
  - **A failed transfer during a remote import is no longer treated as a success.** A ZIP chunk that does not come back cleanly now falls back to per-file fetching, and a 401 stops the whole batch.
  - **A remote import no longer overwrites a rating you set yourself.**
  - **Log streaming and `fleet/update/status` are now behind the "allow remote updates" master switch.** These two were the only endpoints outside it, and stayed reachable while it was off.
  - **Fetching the fleet permission list (my-permissions) is faster.** The identity seed was read from the database once per peer; it is now read once per request.

## [4.679.24] - 2026-08-29

### Fixed

- **Covered the one path missed in the previous timeout fix: `hailort.rs::llm_generate` (the admin diagnostic route) (caught by Codex stop-time review).** The last release unified every native chat/completions/caption path onto `DEFAULT_GENERATE_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`, but this admin route still forwarded `None` to the sidecar whenever the caller omitted `timeout_ms`, leaving the old 30s default active. Added `.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_GENERATE_TIMEOUT_MS)` so an omitted value now falls back to the new default while an explicit caller-supplied value is still capped at `MAX_TIMEOUT_MS`.

## [4.679.21] - 2026-08-29

### Fixed

- **Addressed spurious HAILO_TIMEOUT under low CmaFree.** Real-hardware measurements (see the previous release) showed that under low CmaFree, load+generate can take up to 108s — far past the default 30s — even though the request eventually succeeds, so the default `timeout_ms` was spuriously surfacing HAILO_TIMEOUT. Added `DEFAULT_GENERATE_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000` to `infer_client.rs` and unified every native chat/completions/caption path (two sites in `hailo_genai_chat.rs`, three in `auto_stubs.rs`, and the old 30s constant in `caption_runner.rs`) onto it. Skipped CmaFree-driven dynamic adjustment to avoid the added complexity; this is a fixed-value bump only.

## [4.679.20] - 2026-08-29

### Fixed

- **Closed the `infer_manager::supervise()` shutdown race for real this time (Codex stop-time review, second pass).** The v4.679.11 fix rechecked `stop` and then separately locked the `child` mutex, leaving a window between the two where shutdown could still slip in. Merged the `stop` recheck and the install-or-discard decision into a single `child.lock()` critical section, making it mutually exclusive with shutdown's own "set `stop`, then take the same lock to terminate" sequence. Whichever side acquires the lock first now fully determines the outcome, and neither ordering can orphan a child process.

## [4.679.11] - 2026-08-29

### Fixed

- **Fixed a shutdown race in `infer_manager::supervise()` (caught by Codex stop-time review).** The crash-recovery logic added in v4.679.7 checked the `stop` flag before awaiting `spawn_with_restart` but not after, so if shutdown terminated the old child while a respawn was still in flight, the newly spawned child could be installed into `AppState.infer_child` after shutdown and orphaned. Added a post-respawn `stop` check that terminates the new child on the spot instead of installing it. No dedicated integration test was added for this exact window since it requires a real successful respawn (a working fake sidecar binary); the fix is a straightforward conditional reviewed for correctness.

## [4.679.7] - 2026-08-29

### Fixed

- **Fixed the yu-infer (Hailo sidecar) not recovering after a crash.** `infer_manager::spawn_with_restart` only retries at startup; once healthy, nothing watched the child process afterward, so a runtime crash (OOM-kill, panic, segfault — unrelated to the known CMA non-reclaim issue) left every subsequent request failing until `yu-server` itself was restarted. Changed `AppState.infer_child` to `Arc<Mutex<Child>>` and added `infer_manager::supervise()`, which polls `try_wait()` every 3 seconds and, on death, respawns via the existing `spawn_with_restart` (reusing the same port, auth token, instance id, etc.). Graceful shutdown now sets a new stop flag before terminating the child, so it doesn't race a respawn mid-shutdown. Added a unit test, `supervise_detects_crash_and_attempts_respawn_without_panicking`. The broader sidecar-supervisor design was rejected in review (NO-GO), but this crash-recovery piece — a real defect unrelated to CMA — was fixed independently as called out at the time.

## [4.679.6] - 2026-08-29

### Fixed

- **Re-verified and corrected the Hailo-10H CMA reclaim TODO entries (v4.598.6/677) on real hardware.** From a fresh reboot (confirmed CMA exhaustion at 16 kB and full recovery to 490,608 kB; firmware/driver both vanilla 5.4.0, pin `9537678`), manually launched the current sidecar and ran `POST /v1/infer/llm/generate` repeatedly. CmaFree showed a one-time page-cache-like drop after the first generation (473,904 → 341,616 kB) and then held steady in the 305,000–341,000 kB range rather than decreasing monotonically, so the old "~59 MiB leaked per request" claim did not reproduce (consistent with the misdiagnosis correction in `docs/ja/hailo/HAILO_5_4_0_DRIVER_VANILLA_TRIAL.md`'s fourth trial). **New real issue found**: under low CmaFree, the same prompt's load+generate can take far longer than the default 30s (60–108s), so the default `timeout_ms` spuriously surfaces HAILO_TIMEOUT (status 4). Also reconfirmed that killing the process does not reclaim CMA, and that the device itself stays healthy after a kill (`hailortcli run2 yolov8n` ran at 227 fps normally). See the corresponding `TODO.md` entries for details.

## [4.629.2] - 2026-08-20

### Fixed

- **Fixed `sync_yu_server_mirror.sh` running `rm -rf` on the path named by an unvalidated environment variable.**
  Its work area could be overridden with `MIRROR_WORKDIR`, whose value was passed to deletion without any validation.
  One typo, or a hostile environment, could delete unrelated material.
  This was found by Codex stop-time review: **a defect introduced when this script was added in the previous version**.

- **Removed the class of thing rather than adding validation.** The script now creates its own work area with `mktemp -d`.
  **There is no occasion to delete something that already exists**, concurrent runs do not collide, and `trap ... EXIT`
  cleans up. This is shorter than writing a path-validation gate and has no bypass; `MIRROR_WORKDIR` was removed
  (`mktemp` already provides test isolation).

### Verification

- **Demonstrated it with a canary** — created `/tmp/canary-must-survive`, pointed `MIRROR_WORKDIR` at it,
  and ran it; the canary remained intact.
- Confirmed no regression on the abort path — an old `PUBLIC_RELEASE_REF` detected 41 unpublished files and aborted,
  with 0 temporary directories left behind.
- A normal run reports `no change; mirror already current`, with 0 temporary directories left behind.

## [4.629.0] - 2026-08-20

### Added

- **Made `PUT /api/analysis/servers/{id}` Rust-native.** It had been a 501-returning stub
  (`analysis_servers.rs::update_server_fwd`), with Python’s `core/analysis_api/server_crud.py` `update_server`
  as the implementation. Extracted `do_update` as a pure function, aligned it with `do_add`／`do_remove`, and
  pass through read-modify-write under `settings_lock` and `cleanup_discovery_metadata`.

- **The `legacy-default` path retains encrypted keys as stored.** This is an **intentional difference**.
  Python’s `_legacy_to_entry` calls `decrypt()`, and `update_server` writes that decrypted entry to `config.json`.
  Thus **a plaintext API key remains on disk** (`save_config_json` and `config_io::write` do not re-encrypt; both
  were measured). Rust appends the stored form and leaves decryption to the existing `all_servers` response path.
  The API response is identical; only the on-disk form of the secret differs, and this is safer.

### Fixed

- **Fixed empty `ai_analysis` fabricating a default claude_api entry.** Python’s `_legacy_to_entry` returns `None`
  for falsy `ai_config`, but Rust `all_servers` checked only `is_object()`. Since `{}` is an object, it had generated
  `Claude (claude-sonnet-4-6)`. It caused little harm while read-only, but now that this version makes the write path
  native, `PUT legacy-default` would **write** a nonexistent server into config.

### Changed

- **Updated the ledger (`MIGRATION_PORTFOLIO_STATUS.md`) from measurement.** Added a section explaining a
  **second series — 18 cases where Rust returns 501** — besides “22 Python forwards.” The source of truth is
  `scripts/parity_no_python_known_fails.txt` (30 lines): 18 501 cases and **10 already implemented but FAILing cases**.

- **Do not use the name `auto_stubs.rs` as evidence.** It contains stubs and complete implementations together.
  The 9 `/api/profiles` routes had been recorded as “Rust stub. stub 503.” but are actually complete implementations
  via `write_profile_atomic`; the FAIL is a harness fixture mismatch. `POST /api/scan/resume` is also implemented
  (501 only when `scan_manager` is uninitialized). Marked the allowlist `STALE`; retiring it requires fixing fixtures,
  not handlers.

### Verification

- `analysis_servers::tests::update*`: **14 cases** (8 implementer, 6 supervisor-injected), all passed.
- **Demonstrated catches** — injected 3 faults into production and confirmed the relevant tests failed each time:
  omit the `priority` write (2 FAILED), restore the empty-`ai_analysis` check (1 FAILED), and store a plaintext key
  on the legacy path (1 FAILED). All 14 passed after restoration.
- All 17 `analysis::` cases passed (no regression in `GET /api/analysis/servers`).
- `cargo clippy -p yu-server` had no warnings.

## [4.628.13] - 2026-08-20

### Fixed

- **Fixed the CMA guide declaring a setting dangerous at the beginning but calling it “recommended” in a table below.**
  The guide says at its outset that placing `cma=` in cmdline silences the VC firmware mailbox, yet §2’s failure-mode
  table placed “← **recommended**” on the `cma=512M` row. The table itself did not say that it recorded the cmdline
  method as of 2026-04-15. **A reader who skipped ahead to the table would perform the operation the document called
  dangerous.** This had propagated to all 11 languages.
  Codex stop-time review found it (the v4.628.12 synchronization copied the body only, so this contradiction remained
  in the ja original and was carried unchanged to 10 languages).

- **Framed the table as a historical record and reconnected “recommended” to the current method.** Added a note
  immediately before the table: “This table is a measurement record of the cmdline method as of 2026-04-15. The
  NUMA-boundary-derived limit (512M) remains valid knowledge, but cmdline `cma=` must not be used. The current method
  is `dtoverlay=cma,cma-512`.” Changed the table heading to “(record as of 2026-04-15)” and the end of the
  `cma=512M` row to “← recommended at the time. **Now use `dtoverlay=cma,cma-512`**.”

- **Changed the `cma=512M` notation that meant capacity.** The 4 locations meant “CMA 512 MB,” not a configuration
  string, but the cmdline notation could be mistaken for input to use. Changed them to plain capacity notation;
  retained the `cma=` form only in the historical-record table and removal/check commands.

### Notes

- **The check itself missed the defect.** The checker written for this issue returned OK for all 11 languages, but
  deliberate defect injection showed it missed 2 of 3 cases. Its scan for recommendation wording **excluded the
  inside of tables** (the original defect was inside a table), and its historical-note check only asked whether `>`
  existed, not what it contained. Fixed both, confirmed all 3 defects are detected, then reran it across all languages.

## [4.628.9] - 2026-08-19

### Fixed

- **The trigger of `検証判定則` treated ordinary remeasurement as being stuck.** Codex stop-time review found it.
  The trigger was “fire when a **judgment** based on the same metric appears a second time”; it did not ask for the
  **value** of that judgment. Experiments normally measure one metric repeatedly, so A/B control measurements,
  reproduction checks, and regression tests also reach a count of 2. It was a **rule that misjudged ordinary
  remeasurement as ‘a sign of being stuck.’** Tabletop exercises judged this passing across 4 revisions.

  Two holes chained together during the correction.

  1. It was changed to “the second non-terminal judgment (FAIL / unable to judge) based on the same metric,” but the
     first occurrence in the source case became unable to judge **before measuring the metric** because of a version
     mismatch, so it cannot be read as “a judgment based on the same metric.” FAIL remained only once, at the third
     occurrence, returning to the same non-firing as rev1. Moved the counting unit from metric to investigation, making
     it **narrow by value (non-terminal judgments only), but not by means (regardless of whether the metrics differ)**.
  2. That unit change had not propagated to 3 downstream locations. `事前宣言` and `作業開始宣言.上申引金` made
     users declare the non-key count field “metric name”; the suspension scope in `発火時処置`, “deepening based on
     that metric,” had no unique referent (the first and third occurrences use different metrics); and **without a
     reset condition, the count increased monotonically** (after an investigation reached 2, every later non-terminal
     judgment exceeded the threshold). Aligned the unit term everywhere and added `再発火` (after completing the
     minimum falsification experiment and incorporating it into the judgment criterion, count again from zero. Run the
     experiment in the same work unit as firing, and do not prevent refiring by deferral).

  Also consolidated scope declarations. They had grown to 4 keys, of which `再測ハ引金ニ非ズ` (do not fire no matter
  how many regression tests are repeated) and `引金ノ内` (failure → success → failure counts) gave **opposite
  instructions for the same series**. Since rev6 counts non-terminal judgments only, “measurement itself” and repeated
  PASS were already out of scope and redundant. Consolidated 4 keys into 1 `計数ノ外` key with 3 items to eliminate
  the conflict; moved `同時発火ノ順序` into `諮問接続` and absorbed `verdict符号` into `校正`
  (`前提再審` went from 13 → 8 keys).

  Also added `記録必須.三値全域` (treat a result that fits none of the three values as “unable to judge,” so a gap in
  the mapping is not delegated to real-time judgment) and a 1-line exception to `自動上申則.禁止` (the route reading
  only that rule could not see the exception).

### Docs

- **Added §5.2 and §5.3 to the retrospective document.** §5.2 says: after moving a trigger from subjectivity to
  observation, next ask **what that observation counts**. Observability is necessary, not sufficient. The check is to
  **apply the rule to work it must not stop**. Both I and the tabletop exercises applied it only to the source case
  (work it should stop) and confirmed firing, never to work it should not stop. Moreover, because the 3 judgments in
  the source case all happened to be non-terminal, **this case cannot distinguish a design that counts judgments from
  one that counts dead ends**. The verification fixture did not pose what the rule requires: “what can this metric not
  distinguish?”

  §5.3 says: “**Count completion of a replacement by the concept changed, not the string replaced.**” When changing
  units, an assert confirmed `指標名ト閾値` had 0 occurrences and reported propagation complete; but the rationale
  comment “repeating judgments of the same metric by another means…” remained, while the body said “regardless of
  whether metrics differ” and the rationale retained the old narrow form. The unpropagated unit change recurred once
  in the verification method that had supposedly fixed it.

  The judgment-transition table now has 8 rows, rev1 through rev8 (the table designated by `未発火ノ検分` as its sole
  instrument).

---

## [4.628.8] - 2026-08-19

### Added

- **Institutionalized the retrospective of the investigation process as `検証判定則`.** Incorporated, as a rule in
  `.claude/agent-workflows.yaml` (sections 59 → 60), the retrospective of the HailoRT/driver 5.4.0 CMA verification
  on 2026-08-16–17, where the first through third judgments were wrong and the fourth corrected them. The source case
  is new: `docs/development/development_docs/INVESTIGATION_PROCESS_RETRO_2026_08.md`.

  The root cause was that the criterion “absolute `CmaFree` recovery after the first HEF load” was implicitly
  established while running the experiment and used for 3 judgments without ever being made explicit. Had the
  criterion been written down, review would have seen that a single measurement cannot distinguish memory loss from
  page-cache repurposing of movable pages. The operation that overturned the judgment was only “load once more from
  a low-`CmaFree` state”; it required neither a build, kernel instrumentation, nor a patch, and could have been done
  in the first 10 minutes.

  The rule has 2 bones. (1) Before beginning, state in the investigation document the judgment criterion (metric,
  PASS/FAIL boundary, and **what that metric cannot distinguish**) and assumptions not being doubted. (2) When a
  second judgment relying on the recorded same metric appears, stop deepening and first run a minimum experiment that
  selects and falsifies 1 judgment criterion.

  Put it in the single location `agent-workflows.yaml`; did not write the rule in `QA_HANDOFF.md` (that document is a
  case ledger, and writing it in both makes drift). Opened only the 2 unresolved practical items in §6 of the
  retrospective — changing `acquire_genai`’s prior `CmaFree` check and determining the origin of “rejected by
  HailoRT” in the old forum post — in `(C)` of `QA_HANDOFF.md`.

  Under `予行演習則`, put the design-advisor tabletop exercise through 3 rounds. Both rev1 and rev2 were NO-GO;
  both failed because they chose not to have a threshold-bearing condition. `design-review.yaml` has
  `aggregation: all_must_pass`, and its `escalation_timing_appropriate` requires replacing a trigger based on
  subjective confidence with an observable condition. `自動上申則` thresholds also have a rationale (“1 time is an
  accidental flake, 2 times is a structural problem”) and a calibration mechanism through `accept_rate < 40%`; if the
  number is removed, it is also removed from calibration. Further, rev1’s activation condition **did not fire on the
  source case itself** (the 3 judgment values, “unable to judge / limited tests only / FAIL,” do not literally match).

  Also recorded the history of making the same failure 3 times in one session: writing without checking the delegated
  destination’s instruments. rev1 used the denominator for `仮設敵則`’s rot detection, rev2 used `自動上申則`’s
  accept_rate, and rev3 added a discriminator on the writing side but the reading side (`ledger report` aggregation
  by label_cut) did not separate rules. The third is hardest to find because the writing-side treatment is done, so it
  looks treated.

### Changed

- **Added item 4 to `作業開始宣言.上申引金（着手前宣言）`.** It requires declaring the metric name and threshold
  of `検証判定則.前提再審` before starting. Because the field’s collective provision imposes `自動上申則` treatment
  (unbounded immediate stop) when it fires, explicitly made this item alone follow the exception in
  `検証判定則.発火時処置` (suspend deepening based on that metric and run the minimum falsification experiment first).

- **Added a back-reference to `s1.action` in `.claude/commands/yaml/debug.yaml`.** It tells an investigation in the
  “does not get fixed” / “cause unknown” state to record `検証判定則.記録必須` in its investigation document before
  starting. Without a reference on the side imposing the obligation, the rule is invisible when used.

### Fixed

- **Withdrew 2 opened items because they were already handled, and added “read the actual item before opening it” to
  the rule.** Both CMA-misdiagnosis items opened in `QA_HANDOFF.md` — modifying `acquire_genai`’s prior `CmaFree`
  check and identifying the source of “rejected by HailoRT” in the old forum post — were **already completed** on main:
  the former in v4.620.8 (even with low `CmaFree`, record `acquire_low_cma_observed` and continue the real load;

  `acquire_rejected_low_cma`; failures after reaching factory are status 8, not the host-memory-error status 3).

## [4.628.7] - 2026-08-19

### Fixed

- **An unterminated normal string paired with a later unrelated quote and hid the climb between them**
  (Codex stop-time review, **the seventh time at the same gate**). This is the side where the gate **falls silent**.

      let a = "opened here;      // この行に閉じ引用符が無い

      let p = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).parent().and_then(|q| q.parent());

      let b = "later string";    // この引用符が最初のものを閉じる

  **This is not a lexical-analysis error.** Giving the same input to ast-grep (tree-sitter = the real Rust parser)
  **pairs exactly the same two quotes**. A correct lexer must mask this range. It requires invalid Rust; rewriting
  the scanner an eighth time therefore cannot fix it.

  **The sixth and seventh cases directly contradict each other.** The sixth says “do not report climbs inside a
  multi-line cooked string”; the seventh says “do not hide climbs in that range.” Shape alone cannot distinguish them.
  “Suspect multi-line cooked strings” cannot be adopted — there are **322 legitimate cases** in `crates/`
  (multi-line SQL).

  **Solved it by content, not shape.** Do not mask only when a multi-line cooked string matches `_MANIFEST_ROOT_RE`;
  report it. Measurement: **0 matches** among 322 cases. Production behavior does not change.

  This decision deliberately reverses one fixture in v4.628.6. Since the gate cannot distinguish that range from
  “a hidden real climb,” it must not fall silent but **escalate**. The reason is retained beside the fixture.

  The self-check has 32 cases: 28 regressions from independent verification plus 4 supervisor injections
  (single-line strings still mask / quiet when a manifest exists but has no parent / multi-line raw strings are out
  of scope / SQL strings remain quiet).

## [4.628.6] - 2026-08-19

### Fixed

- **The contents of normal strings spanning multiple lines were scanned as code**
  (Codex stop-time review, **the sixth time at the same gate**). **This time, false positives only.**

  Rust allows `"…"` to span multiple lines. Because scanning ended strings at newlines, second and later lines were
  judged code and reported if they contained something climb-like. It was already correct that an embedded hatch did
  not exempt later content and that a real climb after a closed string was reported.

  Changed the terminator to **only an unescaped `"`**, tracking `\\` and continuation by `\` + newline.

  **Explicitly checked the danger in the opposite direction.** This fix can create false negatives — if a string lacks
  its closing quote, the scan considers itself “inside a string” to end of file and hides a subsequent real climb.
  This is exactly the type encountered in v4.628.5, so fixed the following in tests:

  - a real climb after an unclosed `"` → **reported**

  - do not mistake `"` in comments or `don't` for a string start

  - do not mistake the char literal `'"'` for a string start

  The self-check has 27 cases — all holes across the six rounds plus the 3 opposite-direction cases above.

## [4.628.5] - 2026-08-19

### Fixed

- **byte / C raw strings hid escapes in real code following them**
  (Codex stop-time review, **the fifth time at the same gate**). **Unlike the preceding 4 times, this is a false negative.**

  The preceding 4 times were “an exemption can be forged” — the gate allowed too much. This time, `br#"…"#` and
  similar strings were not parsed correctly, so **a climb in real code after them was not reported at all**. This is
  the side where the gate falls silent, and the worst form. Measurement:

      *** MASKED ***  br#"unpaired " quote"#;  の後の実 climb

      *** MASKED ***  br"unpaired " quote";    の後の実 climb

      *** MASKED ***  cr#"unpaired " quote"#;  の後の実 climb

  **The cause was a condition added in v4.628.3**: “if immediately before a raw-string start is an identifier
  character, it is not a raw string.” It prevented misrecognizing the final `r` of `myvar`, but **`b` and `c` are
  valid Rust prefixes** (`br"…"` / `cr#"…"#`), so the condition was too broad.

  Checked the literal section of the Rust Reference and covered every prefix — `"`, `r`, `b`, `br`, `c`, `cr`,
  char, and byte char. It also handles not mistaking a lifetime `'a` for a char literal and consuming later code,
  and an invalid literal without a closing quote hiding later code.

  > **The decision to stop closing these one at a time had to be made twice.** The fourth time, switching from
  > line-by-line to a whole-file stateful scan appeared to remove the class, but another hole remained: an
  > **incomplete literal vocabulary**. Enumerating from memory misses things (it did). **Consult the specification
  > and cover it exhaustively.**

  The self-check has 21 cases — every hole across the five rounds.

## [4.628.4] - 2026-08-19

### Changed

- **Changed `crate-escapes-root` from line-by-line judgment to one stateful scan of the entire file**
  (Codex stop-time review, **the fourth time at the same gate**).

  The finding was that an exemption could be forged in a multi-line raw string. **After trying 11 forms,
  no form that falsely exempted an actual-code climb could be reproduced** — all 4 exempted forms had the
  climb itself in a string or comment, not actual code.

  It was still fixed because **judging line by line itself** was the problem. Three times, only the reported
  hole had been closed (no reason → string literal → raw string). As long as it is line-by-line, similar forms
  must keep being sought.

  A single scan now determines whether every position is in `code` / a normal string / a raw string
  (multi-line) / a line comment / a block comment (multi-line, nested). On top of that:

  - **report climbs only in `code` regions** — apparent climbs in strings or comments are not actual code,
    so they are not reported (false positives disappeared at the same time)
  - make **hatches valid only in comment regions**

  This removes the whole **class** of “misidentification because it is line-by-line.”

  The self-check has 14 cases, including inside and outside multi-line raw strings, inside and outside
  multi-line block comments, depth counting for nested `/* /* */ */`, and an embedded hatch in a raw string
  not exempting a subsequent climb.

## [4.628.3] - 2026-08-19

### Fixed

- **A raw string could forge a `crate-escapes-root` exemption** (a v4.628.0 defect.
  Detected by Codex stop-time review. **The third time at the same gate**).

  v4.628.2 stated the limitation “do not parse raw strings (`r#\"…\"#`)”, but **that statement itself was wrong**.
  They were not simply unsupported and ignored: an **unpaired `\"` in a raw string flips** parser state,
  making the remainder appear to be “outside the string”:

      let s = r#"unbalanced " quote // crate-escapes-root: <十分に長い理由>"#;

      let p = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).parent().and_then(|q| q.parent());

  Measurement confirmed that **the exemption passed** in the 2 forms `r#"…"#` and `r##"…"##`.
  It was not “merely unparsed,” but **a means of forgery**, so the stated limitation was factually false.

  Changed it to parse raw strings correctly (start with `r` + `#` × N + `"`, end with `"` + `#` × N;
  when immediately preceded by an identifier character, it is not a raw string). Removed the erroneous limitation.

  **Do not write an unverified claim as a limitation.** That left the defect behind this time.

  The self-check has 12 cases — 2 forged forms, a balanced raw string, `r"…"`, normal string literals,
  `//` in strings, `//` and `/* */` comments, empty/short reasons, and preventing false recognition of an
  identifier ending in `r`.

## [4.628.2] - 2026-08-19

### Fixed

- **The `crate-escapes-root` escape hatch also worked inside string literals** (a v4.628.0 defect.
  Detected by Codex stop-time review. **The second “not working” at the same gate**).
  Because it did not inspect **where** on the line the marker occurred, this was exempted:

      let e = err("crate-escapes-root: not a comment, just a string literal");

      let p = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).parent().and_then(|q| q.parent());

  The reason is long enough, so v4.628.1’s 20-character requirement cannot prevent it.

  Made the marker valid **only when in a Rust comment**. Scan each line left-to-right while tracking inside/outside
  `"` strings (including `\"` escapes), and accept markers only after `//` or `/*` **outside strings**.

  **Documented the limitation in a code comment** — raw strings (`r#"…"#`) are not parsed. This is a gate to
  prevent exceptions from slipping in unnoticed, not a defense against deliberate evasion (someone able to edit
  this repo can remove the gate itself). It protects the boundary between “comment” and “code.”

  Added 7 cases to the self-check. In addition to the hole itself (a string literal), it includes a case such as
  `let url = "http://x"; // crate-escapes-root: …` that must **not mistake `//` in a string** for the start of a comment.

## [4.628.1] - 2026-08-19

### Fixed

- **The `crate-escapes-root` escape hatch passed with no reason** (a v4.628.0 defect.
  Detected by Codex stop-time review). Because the judgment was a substring match,
  `if "crate-escapes-root:" not in line`, **writing only `// crate-escapes-root:` silenced it**.

  The point of the hatch is to make anyone adding an exception **write a reason**. Allowing an empty marker lets
  a future contributor pass it without thinking. This is the “the gate exists but does not work” form.

  Extract the text after the colon and require **at least 20 characters** after whitespace is removed.
  If it does not meet that requirement, do not recognize it as an escape hatch; report it including
  `justification too short` (merely reporting “escape” would not tell its author that the reason is insufficient).

  Added **this hole itself** to the self-check as fixtures — no reason / whitespace only / 1 character.
  All are confirmed detected. The current 2 sites pass because they have long English text.

## [4.628.0] - 2026-08-19

### Added

- **Added a gate that prohibits `crates/` from escaping outward** (`crate-escapes-root`; gates 54 → 55).
  Since `crates/` is mirrored to `eauesque/yu-server` and reviewed independently, it **must not escape outward**
  (it is fine for the outer repo to refer into `crates/`, since `crates/` is bundled with yu_ai_manager).

  Existing `crate-include-paths` checks only **path strings** in `include_str!` / `include_bytes!`.
  But the defect found in v4.627.0 was a climb **during tests**: `cargo check` and `cargo build` passed, while
  **only running `cargo test` in the extracted tree failed 5 cases**. A static include check cannot catch it in principle.

  The new gate counts chains of `.parent()` originating at `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`. Every crate is directly under
  `crates/<name>`, so **one climb is allowed inside `crates/`; 2 or more are rejected as escape**.
  `.and_then(|p| p.parent())` is counted as obtaining a parent too.

  **Confirmed firing by fault injection in 3 directions** — (1) restoring v4.627.0’s `repo_root()` fails,
  (2) increasing `detect.rs`’s `.parent()` from 1 to 2 fails (proof that the boundary works), and
  (3) removing the escape-hatch comment fails (proof that the hatch works).

- Added reasoned escape hatches to the 2 existing escapes. `test_state()` in `mcp_client.rs` and
  `comfyui_bridge.rs` directs `project_root` to the repo root, but that is **intentional** — both are tests
  comparing against Python implementations (under `extensions/`), which have no counterpart in the mirror alone.
  In fact, `comfyui_bridge`’s `delete_model_registry_entry_refuses_builtin_without_override` is one of the
  5 cases that fail in the extracted tree.

  > Of the 3 reported sites, `hailo_yolo_stream/detect.rs` was **a false positive by the gate**.
  > It calls `.parent()` only once and reads `crates/Cargo.toml`, remaining inside `crates/`.
  > Escape is not “calling `.parent()`” but “**climbing 2 or more levels upward**.”

## [4.626.2] - 2026-08-19

### Fixed

- **Aligned capacity-limit judgement with Python and made the test pass through the seam** (closing the first `Known gaps` item from v4.626.0). Rust used `reqwest::Response::content_length()`, which returns a **body size hint**. Python reads the **header** with `_content_length(resp.headers)`. Added `hf_declared_content_length()` to read the `Content-Length` header directly. This follows Python and is testable. Headerless chunked responses remain covered by the accumulated in-stream check.

## [4.626.1] - 2026-08-19

### Fixed

- **Fixed concurrent downloads sharing a temporary file and being able to permanently cache a corrupt model** (a v4.626.0 defect found in Codex stop-time review). `download_hf_file` used `{name}.{pid}.tmp`, which was always identical for the same destination in one process. With two concurrent downloads, (1) both `File::create` calls truncate each other, (2) writes interleave, and (3) `rename` can put a **partial file at the destination**. Since `cached` checks only existence, not content, **a corrupt model can then keep being returned as cached forever**.

  Extracted temporary-path generation into `hf_temporary_path()`, added an `AtomicU64` counter, and now use `{name}.{pid}.{seq}.tmp`. Each download writes its own temporary file; `rename` replaces only complete files with last-writer-wins semantics. **The test fails when the counter is fixed to 0.** A comment explains that because cached trusts only existence, temporary-path uniqueness is the sole protection against corruption.

  ⚠ **The Python side (`model_download.py:281`) has the same defect.** It uses `os.getpid()`, so the same collision can occur. It is possible in Python coexistence mode and has been filed in `TODO.md`.

  SSRF protection ports every Python `_hf_request` rule (`model_download.py:84`): http/https only; **reject URLs containing userinfo**; exact host match for `huggingface.co` / `hf.co` or `"." + allowed` suffix match; **do not automatically follow redirects and revalidate every hop** (limit 5); mandatory User-Agent. It builds on the existing `analysis_engines/http_client.rs::build_pinned_client`, which **pins resolved IPs to prevent DNS rebinding** (stronger than Python). `allow_local` is fixed to false.

  Also added protection Python lacks: `files[].name` comes from profile JSON and is part of the destination path, so each destination is verified by canonicalisation to be under the model directory.

## [4.625.1] - 2026-08-19

### Fixed

- **Fixed retag cancellation taking effect up to 63 items late** (a v4.625.0 defect found in Codex stop-time review). `run_batch_worker_with_tagger` checked cancellation with `idx % cancel_every == 0`; retag passed `cancel_every = batch_size` (up to 64). ⟹ **Up to 63 extra files could be tagged after cancellation.** Batch passed `1`, so it was unaffected.

  **The cause was in the porting spec itself.** Python checks at chunk boundaries because `adapter.tag_images_batch(paths, batch_size)` processes **one chunk in one inference call** and cannot be interrupted midway. Rust calls `call_wd_infer` one item at a time, so chunking brings no inference benefit and only delays cancellation. Copying Python's shape without checking why it exists was the error.

  Removed `cancel_every` and check the token **before every file** (identically for batch and retag). `batch_size` remains validated for API compatibility ([1,64] outside is 400), but is unused at runtime. Replaced the incorrect note that it was intentionally cancellation granularity with an explanation of the above. Added a test that immediately cancels 64 targets and pins processing to at most one; it fails if restored to `idx % 64`.

## [4.625.0] - 2026-08-19

### Fixed

- **Fixed a pre-existing bug where `/api/search-grouped` returned 500 for conditional searches** (a by-product of the retag port). `fetch_matching_ids` (`search.rs`) built from `"SELECT f.id FROM files f WHERE "`, while following `push_where_filters` starts with **`" AND f.is_deleted=0"`** (`search.rs:638`). The resulting SQL was `WHERE  AND f.is_deleted=0 …`, a **SQLite syntax error**. Every `search_grouped` request with `has_conditions` true (`q`, `tag`, `wd_model`, etc.) returned 500. **It shipped because there was no test**—the only two existing tests built their own `WHERE 1=1` builder and did not use this path. Changed the root to `WHERE 1=1` and added a conditional `search_grouped` regression test. **Reverting only the production line makes that test fail while its helper builder remains intact.**

- **Resolved the `wd_tagger` job-ID split brain** (`todo(bug/wd-tagger)` in TODO.md). `POST /api/wd-tagger/batch` is Rust-native and starts `"wd_tagger"` in `state.job_manager`, while `retag/{batch,backfill,query}` forwarded to Python and started the same ID in Python's `job_manager`. Since `start_if_idle` in separate maps in separate processes cannot see the other, **mutual exclusion of “only one at a time” was broken**, and `retag/cancel` and `batch/cancel` shared an ID without being able to stop each other. Making retag async Rust-native and using the same job ID in the same `JobManager` gives both mutual exclusion and cancellation **structurally**.

### Added

- **Made `retag/{batch,backfill,query,cancel}` Rust-native** (removed Python forwarding). Remaining Python dependencies: **28 → 24** (`rust-python-forwarders.txt`). The Python implementation remains; removal follows parity verification.
  - The worker reuses existing `run_batch_worker_with_tagger` (already generalised by tagger function). Inference through writing uses a common function extracted from native `retag_single`.
  - backfill's `NOT EXISTS` resolves and uses the **model_id from the request body**, not the active configured model. `query_backfill_targets` now takes the model argument; a test pins down that batch continues to use the configured model.
  - `query` scope uses **policy C** (user decision, 2026-08-19): changed targets from “one page of search results” to “**all records matching the search criteria**.” It does not touch `search()`, so regex-search and folder-sort post-processing divergence cannot arise in principle. **This is a behaviour change.**
  - `query_params` arrives as a JSON object while every `SearchQueryRaw` field is `Option<String>` (for query strings), so numbers and booleans such as `{"limit":50}` failed deserialisation. This is a **conversion layer easily missed in a port**; scalars are normalised to strings.
  - retag/query directly call `fetch_matching_ids`, bypassing `search()`'s preconditions (empty if `files` is absent; drop `also_path` if `files_path_fts` is absent). Added equivalent guards on the retag side. **Tests fail if the guards are removed.**

### Changed

- Response envelope: the four retag paths wrap with `api_result(json!({"data": {...}}))`, matching Python. `api_result` puts payload keys at top level and leaves `data` null, so without the wrapper `body["data"]["status"]` is null. Also fixed this wrapper being lost during sharing, which regressed existing test `retag_single_native_success_uses_sanitized_model_and_nested_data`.

- **Registered one intentional parity difference** (ENDPOINTS in `verify_rust_compat.py`). Rust rejects an unknown `model_id` first with **404 `model_not_found`** (the same contract as `retag_single`). Python starts the job and fails while loading the engine. The Rust side is correct, so the difference remains; 404 was added to accepted statuses with a reason. It surfaced only when the forwarding became native—while forwarding, they necessarily matched.

### Fixed

Sibling `sd_webui_bridge.rs:68` has the correct order. No current caller contains these keys, but it was a latent mine.

Axum and Quart both return 405 for a matching path with the wrong method, so it now expects 405 with an explanation.

The cause was structural: broad `data/` (and later `*.key`) rules in `.gitignore` swallowed the key, so **the golden vector's key was not in the repo**. A new clone has no `data/` at all and could not pass in principle.

### Added

- **`scripts/internal/gen_secret_store_fixture.py` (fixture generator).** It points `TAGDB_DATA_DIR` at the fixture (Rust reads the same variable, so Rust reads where Python writes), explicitly removes `YU_SECRET_PASSPHRASE` (if retained, key derivation uses the passphrase path and silently produces a fixture others cannot decrypt), fixes the key ID (avoiding regeneration diffs), and has production `secret_store.encrypt()` create v2 tokens. As a **self-check**, Python reads back what it wrote before writing it out; otherwise Rust would chase a phantom defect from a fixture Python itself cannot decrypt. The key is test-only, encrypts only literal `python-fixture-secret`, and protects nothing.

## [4.622.0] - 2026-08-17

### Fixed

- **Wired the gateway scope gate (L3) into the SD proxy.** `sd_handler` in `crates/yu-server/src/routes/gateway_proxy.rs` had loopback, Origin, and path-allowlist layers but **never called `check_request` or `has_scope`**, while being production-wired as `/sd/sdapi/v1/{*sub}` (`main.rs:3157`). Thus any loopback process could call `POST /sdapi/v1/options` (switching the running model) without a gateway key; even a key with only `sd:query` could pass as `sd:admin`; and `gateway.auth.allow_loopback_bypass: false` was ignored.
  - **The defect was not “forgot to write the gate” but “lost the mapping in the port.”** Python's `core/gateway/sd_proxy.py:SD_ALLOWED_ENDPOINTS` is `dict[(method, path) -> Scope]`, assigning `sd:generate` / `sd:query` / `sd:admin` to 20 paths. Rust ported it as `&[(&str, &str)]`, dropping **only the Scope column** and leaving a plain allowlist. Restored the triples and added `sd_scope_for()` (Python `get_sd_scope` equivalent).
  - **Judgement order matches Python** (`routes/gateway_sd.py:179-198`): Origin → path → scope lookup (unregistered is **404**, answered before auth so unauthenticated callers cannot enumerate proxied paths) → `check_request` → `has_scope`. L3 is **before reading the body**, avoiding paying for unbounded uploads on rejected requests. `allow_loopback_bypass` honours its config value as Python does.
  - comfy/gradio/agentmemory have no Rust proxy handlers, fall back to Python (503 standalone), and Python already gates all four paths; the hole was SD only.
  - Some deployments have a **behaviour change**: users with `gateway.auth.allow_loopback_bypass: false` and the Rust SD proxy now need a key with `sd:generate`, `sd:query`, or `sd:admin`; previously they passed with no key. Default deployments (bypass enabled) are unchanged, pinned by `sd_without_bearer_still_works_by_default`.

### Added

- **Nine SD scope-gate tests.** Core coverage: (1) an `sd:query` key gets 403 `insufficient_scope` for `POST /sdapi/v1/options` (restoring two-tuples makes this pass); (2) an `sd:generate` key cannot reach query/admin paths; (3) unregistered paths are **404**, not 401 even without a key, pinning order; (4) rejected requests do not read the body (a body that errors when read still yields 401); (5) a test actually reads Python `sd_proxy.py` and compares mappings (widening either side fails; count-equality assertion also catches silent parser failures).
  - Confirmed detection with three fault injections: disabling `has_scope` fires 2 tests; weakening the table (admin→query) fires 3 (including mapping comparison); breaking 404→401 order fires 1.

## [4.620.12] - 2026-08-17

### Fixed

- **Fixed all route-side configuration reads becoming empty and writes overwriting TOML with JSON in `config.toml` deployments.** `main.rs` put existing `config.toml` into `AppState` as `config_path`, but `config_io::load()` ignored its extension and read with `serde_json`. Configuration therefore became an empty object, then `config_io::write()` wrote JSON over `config.toml`, leaving invalid TOML on next startup. It now branches by extension and reads/writes TOML as TOML. Values TOML cannot represent (`null`) **reject the write**, preserving existing configuration rather than silently dropping it.
- **Restored background-job elapsed time to the bottom progress bar and made it tick every second.** Rendering had already moved to `nav/job-progress-ui.ts` but did not render elapsed time; the old supposed root cause, `scan-banner/ui-render.ts`, had zero callers. Poll values and `Date.now()` anchor a ticker extrapolation, re-anchored on the next poll. SSE `elapsed_seconds: 0` does not re-anchor or reset the running clock; the final value freezes on completion. Removed dead `ui-render.ts` and `ui-utils.ts`.

### Changed

- **Eliminated all yu-server `include_str!` references crossing the repo root** (a separation prerequisite): three files, eight measured sites. The two production sites in `misc_admin.rs` now read at runtime; configuration schema reuses existing `routes::settings::schema_path()`, and extension manifests read from `extensions/<name>/extension.json` (same default on absence). Moved golden fixtures to `crates/yu-server/tests/fixtures/`; extension-template tests now read at runtime (skip only if `extensions/` itself is absent; fail if it exists but the file is missing).

### Added

- **A gate against `include_str!` crossing crate boundaries** (`scripts/internal/crate_include_paths.py`). Cargo does not treat `include_str!` as a dependency, so cross-boundary usage can pass both build and test. It checks both bare relative paths and `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), …)` forms; fault injection confirmed it fires.
- **A gate catching endpoints that silently disappear from documentation.** `check_native_only_endpoints.py` inspected only `rust_module` entries listed by the manifest itself. It reads committed generated `docs/ja/api/all-endpoints.md` from HEAD as a baseline and treats paths that are “in the baseline, absent from current generated output, and still provided by Rust” as violations. Flask/Axum path notation differences are normalised; its self-check catches a change that kills normalisation.

- **Implemented and disproved the missing-`FOLL_LONGTERM` hypothesis on real hardware.** Based on v4.620.6's hypothesis that `prepare_sg_table()` used `get_user_pages()` without `FOLL_LONGTERM`, actually replaced it with `pin_user_pages(FOLL_WRITE | FOLL_FORCE | FOLL_LONGTERM)` + `unpin_user_page()`, completed build, DKMS re-registration, and hardware load, then reran the same repro (`tools/diag_hailo_cma_reclaim.py`) from post-reboot high `CmaFree` (453 MB). Only 10 MB of 273 MB consumed returned: **no change at all from before (`VERDICT: FAIL` continues)**. `dmesg` confirmed `pin_user_pages` ran without error. Forced compaction (`vm.compact_memory`) also had no effect; `MemAvailable` remained healthy at 7.1 GB while only `CmaFree` failed to recover. **The missing-`FOLL_LONGTERM` hypothesis is theoretically valid as a Linux-kernel practice violation, but was not the root cause of this observed symptom.** Recorded eliminated causes (driver `dma_alloc_coherent` path, SG map/destroy mismatch, SWIOTLB, `FOLL_LONGTERM`) and next directions (a HailoRT userspace-buffer allocator cause; direct observation with `CONFIG_CMA_DEBUGFS`/`page_owner`). - **Rebuilt pyhailort for 5.4.0 and reran the existing CMA repro (`tools/diag_hailo_cma_reclaim.py`) on real hardware, confirming the CMA non-release issue also reproduces on v5.4.0** (driver/library/firmware/pyhailort all self-built and version-matched), with `VERDICT: FAIL`. Installed the pyproject in `hailort/libhailort/bindings/python/platform/` (scikit-build-core + pybind11) into `.venv`, explicitly linking the existing `/usr/local` build through `LIBHAILORT_PATH` / `HAILORT_INCLUDE_DIR` (`ldd` confirmed `libhailort.so.5.4.0`). Using the same method and HEF (Qwen3-1.7B-Instruct) as 2026-05, child-process VDevice/LLM load → `SIGTERM` → 30-second wait consumed 137 MB and reclaimed -22 MB (`CmaFree` stayed around 512 kB minutes later), qualitatively the same result as 5.3.0. v5.4.0 does not fix it; next is considering a local patch to GPL-2.0 public driver sources.

- **Wired HailoRT native tool-call support into the Hailo prompt-based agent** (TODO(hailo-genai) phase 1). Verified `LLMGenerator::write(messages, tools)` in `yu-hailo-infer` (another repo, pushed private and public, pin rev updated) on real hardware using Qwen3-1.7B-Instruct.hef: the model responds in `<tool_call>{"name":...,"arguments":...}</tool_call>` form, already parseable by the existing regex. ## [4.620.6] - 2026-08-17

### Docs

- **Identified and recorded the root cause of the Hailo-10H CMA non-release problem.** Replaced unsafe page inspection such as `virt_to_page()` with safe instrumentation (only existing atomic-counter and allocation-size output through `dev_err()`), then reproduced and analysed on real hardware. Driver allocations through `dma_alloc_coherent()` (descriptor lists and continuous buffers) were only a few MB and not the cause. The path mapping userspace-allocated memory for DMA (`hailo_vdma_buffer_map()`, `HAILO_DMA_USER_PTR_BUFFER`) handles many 8 MB buffers when loading Qwen3-1.7B-Instruct. Source tracing found `prepare_sg_table()` calls `get_user_pages(FOLL_WRITE | FOLL_FORCE)` **without `FOLL_LONGTERM`**. This violates documented Linux-kernel practice for long DMA transfers (`pin_user_pages()` + `FOLL_LONGTERM`): if userspace pages that happen to be in CMA are pinned, CMA migration cannot work and they are not immediately recognised as free CMA after release, fully matching the measurements. Recorded a candidate replacement with `pin_user_pages` + `FOLL_LONGTERM`, but it was not yet verified on hardware. Details: §7 of `HAILO_5_4_0_DRIVER_VANILLA_TRIAL.md`; next was to reflect this in a Hailo forum post and, if possible, try the fix.

## [4.620.1] - 2026-08-16

### Fixed

- **Completely rewrote tool-call extraction in `parse_tool_call_with_known_names` so real-hardware output from Qwen3-1.7B-Instruct can be parsed correctly.** Found while re-verifying the v4.620.0 native tool wiring: the model sometimes returns `{"arguments": {...}, "name": "..."}` (the reverse order, with `arguments` before `name`) with `<|im_end|>` directly appended, which old order-dependent regexes (`TOOL_CALL_RE`/`TOOL_CALL_SIMPLE_RE`) could not parse. Replaced them entirely with a single-pass O(n) `extract_json_objects()` helper that tracks brace depth on a stack, correctly ignores braces in string literals, and is order-independent.
  - **Converged after three further Codex stop-time-review findings**: (1) giving up when the first candidate is not a tool call misses a valid later one → scan all candidates; (2) the simple repair for (1), rescanning one character after an unterminated `{`, becomes O(n²) → fundamentally changed to one pass that pushes opening positions and records on close; (3) limiting candidates by fixed count can discard the tail of valid sibling candidates → limit by cumulative parsed-character budget (`text.len()*4` or more). Sibling candidates total at most O(n), so all are tried without exhausting budget; only duplicated deeply nested candidates consume it quickly and stop.
  - Confirmed all 33 `cargo test -p yu-server` tests (including new regressions), zero clippy warnings, and `pre_push_check.py`. Details: `QA_HANDOFF.md` (A-2).

## [4.599.1] - 2026-08-08


### Security

- **Upgraded vulnerable dependencies across 3 systems.** The 38 warnings collapse to 11 packages when duplicates are folded. There are zero PRs—the setting disables PRs in the private repo, and the 22 dependabot branches remained without being converted to PRs. We split into 3 passes per system (splitting prevents comb-back if one breaks).
  - **rust**: `quinn-proto` 0.11.14 → 0.11.16. Passed 511 tests in lan-cowork.
  - **pip**: `pillow` 12.2.0 → 12.3.0 (direct dependency), `aiohttp` 3.14.1 → 3.14.3, `cryptography` 49.0.0 → 50.0.0, `h2` 4.3.0 → 4.4.1 (and `hpack` followed). Since `pillow` is the body of image processing, we ran actual PNG/WebP round-trips and downscaling to verify; 357 image tests passed (5 failures are all playwright browser missing, unrelated to this change).
  - **npm**: `undici` 7.28.0 → 7.29.0, `hono` 4.12.32 → 4.13.1, `fast-uri` 3.1.4 → 3.1.5, `dompurify` 3.4.11 → 3.4.13 (the only direct dependency). Build and TS tests passed 122 cases.

### Discovered

- **`nanoid` and `postcss` are intentionally not upgraded.** The chain is `nanoid ← postcss ← vite ← vitest ← devDependencies`, and **does not appear in production distribution**. Upgrading `vitest` to 4.1.10 causes `vite` 8.0.16 to keep demanding an old version. We can force it with `pnpm.overrides`, but that **overwrites the test runner's internal dependencies**, making breakage hard to trace, and the gain is only dev-dependency warning cleanup—we decline it.
- **`quinn-proto` returns empty from `cargo tree -i`**—it does not exist in the current build graph; a version simply remained in `Cargo.lock`. There was never risk. **The warning-without-consumer type exists.**
- ⟹ **22 branches ≠ 38 warnings.** Some branches do not have warnings (transitive dependencies), some warnings exist without branches (phantom dependencies in the lock).

### Added

The resolution order matches Python's `_resolve_group_id()` at `device_manager.py:55-67`: **env `HAILO_VDEVICE_GROUP_ID` > config `hailo.vdevice_group_id` > `"YU_SHARED"`**. Python uses `if env:`, so **empty strings pass through to config**—we replicated this behavior (a naive `env::var().unwrap_or(...)` would differ).

Resolving from the merged side causes **the value to diverge under deployments that use profile**, breaking silent sharing. We followed the existing distinction shown by the comment at line 684, "Deliberate asymmetry."

## [4.598.11] - 2026-08-08


### Added

- **Implemented Hailo sidecar model residency (3 stages, CI green).** Spec at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-sidecar-single-vdevice-design.md` (rev4, GO. rev1–rev3 were NO-GO; each revision's error remains in §0/§0b). Sidecar commits: `5418143` (stage 1) → `e64c6de` (stage 2) → `084374e` (stage 3).
  - **Stage 1: One VDevice per process, with group_id.** Previously, we called `VDevice::create_shared()` at 4 sites per type without arguments. Two VDevices in the same process fail with `74`; **even with the same group_id, separate instances cause `InferModel.run()` to fail with "not configured as view"** (measured in `hailo_vdevice_concurrent_2026-04-06.md:198-206`). We do not release—`VDevice.release()` does not return CMA, so release does nothing.
  - **Stage 2: Dedicated device thread.** The handle is `NonNull` and `!Send`, so creation-and-discard inside `spawn_blocking` will not persist residency. We replaced the global mutex with a handle-owning thread, converted `run_hailort_task` to `FnOnce(&mut DeviceCtx)`, and rewrote **14 paths (12 + 2 streaming)** accordingly. **Only the closure and result cross the thread boundary**, so no `unsafe impl Send` is needed (we added zero).
  - **Stage 3: Residency.** The key is full create arguments. Tolerance rules span 2 stages—InferModel class (`ShimYolo`) permits parallel existence of other HEFs (both `clip-image` and `yolo/detect` pass both as different HEFs; first-come-first-served would break one forever), GenAI class operates 1 at a time, and swapping HEFs appends the current HEF to reject with 409. `Speech2Text` has no `clear_context`, so we do not make it resident.

### Fixed

- **Residency nearly broke the feature it improves.** HailoRT **accepts system role only when context is empty**. Each turn, the caller stacks system and resends the latest 20 turns; today's create-per-bill keeps context always empty so it does not break. **Reusing the handle breaks on turn 2**—already found and fixed on hardware (`HAILO_LLM_SUBPROCESS_DEVLOG.md` §7, commit `cdd9e26fe`). ⟹ **Call `clear_context()` after every generation.** Also: without clear, turn B's context gets stacked on turn A's live context (under LAN Cowork, this can cross users). **The test seized this in live demonstration** (drop clear → 2 failures; restore → 63 passed).
- **Silenced 4 FFI redeclaration warnings from stage 1 tests** (bundled in stage 2). The second declaration coinciding today will be a different second tomorrow; moreover, this is **the one FFI gap the compiler can catch**—a future mismatch will not show.

### Discovered

- **My verification command lacked `--all-targets`, leaving the test profile unlinted.** The 4 warnings existed behind the "passed" label. **CI has no hole (includes `--all-targets`), and stage 1's push actually failed. I did not see it and moved on.** Henceforward `--all-targets` is default.

### Remaining

- **C++ API shape remains unverified** (`HailoRTDefaults::get_vdevice_params()` / `params.group_id`). SDK headers are unavailable locally; real shim compiles only on Pi. If wrong, it fails there.
- **~14 MB/min sustained leak during inference does not disappear with residency.** It is a separate path, independent of load/unload; mitigation is the existing auto-reboot mechanism (Phase 0.5).
- Pin update held (decision 2026-08-08). The pin targets the public mirror and development is private, so sync is required. We defer to public release for bulk handling.

## [4.598.10] - 2026-08-08


### Fixed

- **The two shim implementations in the sidecar each declared the shared C ABI independently; changing one silently broke** (sidecar `0eeb65d`). `build.rs` switches between `shim.cpp` / `shim_stub.cpp` depending on SDK presence, but `extern "C"` includes neither arity nor type in the symbol name, so **adding an argument to one compiles, links, and tests pass on both—then silently breaks at runtime (undefined behavior)**. We consolidated POD 3 types, opaque 6 types, all 30 declarations into `src/hailort/shim.h`; both implementations include it. **The joint is sealed—confirmed in action** (changing only the header arity → `conflicting declaration of C function` build error; restore → green). **Only the C++ sides (2 faces) are sealed; the Rust `ffi.rs` remains hand-written**, noted at the header top.

### Rejected

- **Solo group_id design is NO-GO.** Four fact-checks were true; the inference was wrong. (1) **"FFI gets type-checked" is false**—as shown above, declarations were not shared (handled in `0eeb65d`). (2) **group_id is not a prerequisite for residency**—the measurement in `hailo_vdevice_concurrent_2026-04-06.md` says "same group_id, separate VDevice: generate succeeds but `InferModel.run()` fails with 'not configured as view'"; the 4-site generate design **is the configuration that the document says does not work**. The true prerequisite is **VDevice unification**, already named in sidecar residency spec §12/§13. ⟹ **group_id and residency are part of the same change**.
- Also, corrections: group_id absence is a recorded decision (M3, "VDevice open failure is the detector"), and reversing it means accepting the loss of the detector / "CMA ceiling does not move" contradicts the measurement "131 MB for cold-spawn VDevice construction alone" / what matters is not resolution **order** but resolution **value consistency**—**yu-server reads config.toml, Python reads config.json**, different sources.
- Positive correction: simultaneous hailo-ollama (C++ binary, same API + env group_id) with Python is **proven by lsof** but unverified is our params construction alone. However the same test **measures an ×8.08 slowdown** (CLIP 18.8 → 152 ms), concluding GenAI parallel-forbid.

## [4.598.9] - 2026-08-08


### Discovered

- **Model switching is not "expensive"—it is "impossible."** `HAILO_CMA_LEAK_HAILORT_5_3_0.md` §3-1–§3-2: after reboot CmaFree ≈ 480 MB, one LLM load ≈ 190 MB, **a second load is permanently impossible**. The same doc §3-2 concludes "multi-model UX is architecturally unsupported in HailoRT 5.3.0." **One GenAI model / Pi reboot is the ceiling.** The residency design's "eviction on switch" dissolves—no switch exists.
- **The sidecar passes no `group_id` at all.** `shim.cpp:293, 395, 501, 758` call `VDevice::create_shared()` with no arguments; the sidecar contains no group_id. This causes two simultaneous problems: (1) **no residency**—keeping an LLM while calling YOLO/CLIP causes a second VDevice to fail with `HAILO_OUT_OF_PHYSICAL_DEVICES(74)` (`VDEVICE_SHARING_PATTERN.md` TL;DR). Create/drop presently finishes inside the lock, hiding it. (2) **hybrid device contention with Python**—group_id crosses processes (`HAILO_DEVICE_CONTROL.md`); Python holds `YU_SHARED`, so different group_ids cannot share. This is today's default configuration; worth hardware verification (unverified).
- **Yet 2× InferModel (YOLO + CLIP) + 1× GenAI can coexist.** `VDEVICE_SHARING_PATTERN.md` has proof on 5.2.0/5.3.0. ROUND_ROBIN time-shares on the same shared VDevice. Constraint: one GenAI max.
- **Conclusion flipped: residency is not a performance gain but the only shape that works.** Per-bill create with constraints means one request per boot practically (`HAILO_CMA_LEAK_HAILORT_5_3_0.md`). The "2-turn exhaustion" measurement is consistent.

### Fixed

- **`HAILO_CMA_LEAK_HAILORT_5_3_0.md` §4's mid-term plan pointed to option (A) subprocess isolation, listed REJECTED in the same table.** This was a dangling line from before Phase 0 PoC. What was actually adopted is (D) auto-reboot, implemented as Phase 0.5. **This one sentence caused "process restart returns CMA"-type designs to be written again on 2026-08-08.**

### Documented

- Fixed Rust sequence: (1) pass group_id to sidecar (prerequisite for all else; solo also fixes coexistence. C++ overload unverified—SDK headers missing), (2) create-once residency (no switch = no slots, no eviction), (3) join the auto-reboot mechanism (do not design new), (4) align `model/unload` parity target to Python actual behavior (unimplementable—declined).

Also reflected: the setting location has since moved from the cmdline to `dtoverlay=cma,cma-512` in `config.txt`. (2) "Plan to restart the process on CMA exhaustion" was disproven by the 2026-05-17 Phase 0 PoC.
- **The same README's file list had 9 entries, but there are actually 15 files.** The 5 missing entries included `HAILO_CMA_LEAK_HAILORT_5_3_0.md` and `HAILO_AUTO_REBOOT_PHASE05.md` — the two most decisive documents in this area.

Both were NO-GO at review.

### Withdrawn

- **Withdrew the v4.598.7 conclusion that "about 83% comes back after the process exits."** The basis was a single post-hoc reading (`CmaFree 158,016 kB`), from which it was not possible to identify when or what returned it. In contrast, `HAILO_CMA_LEAK_HAILORT_5_3_0.md` §2-1 measured, **independently twice**, on the same physical device, SIGTERM + join + 30 seconds → **only +8 MB recovered** (expected ≥250 MB), and concluded that recovery happens "neither on process exit, nor on kill, nor on module unload." **The measurement itself remains valid and is not withdrawn. What was wrong was the interpretation.** Along with this, the floor of "once created, never discard; switching is done via sidecar restart" is also withdrawn — if a restart does not reclaim memory, there is no means of switching.
- **The sidecar supervision design is NO-GO.** In addition to the reason above, review independently raised 4 must-fix items. Notably, the trigger cannot see the failure it is meant to catch (streaming returns 200 before `Llm::create`, and errors appear as SSE inside a 200 body, so `InferClientError` never occurs). Only the crash-recovery portion will be resubmitted separately, as a genuine defect unrelated to CMA.

## [4.598.7] - 2026-08-08


### Measured

- **`CmaFree` after process exit was 158,016 kB. Of the 60,160 kB leaked, about 49,936 kB (about 83%) came back.** Against a baseline of 168,240, 10,224 kB is still short. In other words, **CMA dropped inside a still-running process is not reclaimed, but most of it is reclaimed once that process exits**. However, since this was a single-point measurement, it was not possible to separate when it was reclaimed (delayed reclaim vs. process exit) from whether the residual 10 MiB is a true residual leak or a separate allocation made in the interim.

### Discovered

- **The defect got smaller, but it still does not recover automatically.** The remedy is "restart the sidecar," not restart the machine. **But nothing restarts it** — `infer_manager::spawn_with_restart(..., 5)` is a startup-time retry loop (until healthy, `infer_manager.rs:103`), and performs no supervision while running. CMA exhaustion does not kill the sidecar; `Llm::create` merely fails while the process keeps standing healthy. So after roughly 2 turns, every subsequent LLM request fails outright, and **there is no recovery until `yu-server` itself is restarted**.

### Decided

- **A working floor for the resident design has been established; proceeding to rev3.** If discarding never gets the memory back, don't discard — build each model into the process exactly once and hold it for the process's lifetime. Only switching requires eviction, and true eviction is only via process restart. **This finally gives `model/unload` an honest implementation** (restarting the sidecar child; `yu-server` already holds `infer_child`). The constraint is "the set of models loaded simultaneously must fit within CMA's 512 MiB." The shared-VDevice spike remains meaningful but is no longer load-bearing. Spec is on the sidecar side, §13, `5fc4d30`.

---

## [4.598.6] - 2026-08-08


### Measured

- **CMA is not reclaimed. One create → drop cycle left 60,160 kB (≈59 MiB) unreturned.** Measured on the physical Hailo-10H with `Llama3.2-1B-Instruct.hef`, with nothing else using Hailo (`CmaTotal 524288 kB`, baseline `CmaFree 168240 kB`, cycle 0 at `108080 kB`). The safety floor triggered at cycle 0, and the hardware was protected. Therefore the resident design's core mechanism, "discard then recreate on mismatch," frees nothing, and cannot be written in that form.
- **One cycle took 34.2 seconds.** This is 6x the earlier 5.86 seconds, even though this round's work was lighter and the hardware was in a cleaner state. There is exactly one structural difference — this round's timing wraps the drop. If that is the cause of the difference, **the release itself takes about 28 seconds, and the memory still is not returned** (this is an inference, since the two measurements were not otherwise controlled for identical conditions).

### Discovered

- **This is a defect in the current implementation, prior to any design question.** `chat_send_native` calls the sidecar path, which creates a handle per request. At 59 MiB per request, a 512 MiB pool, and 164 MiB free at the start of measurement, **the native chat path exhausts CMA in roughly 2 turns**. This is not a performance problem but a "does not function in production" problem, and it exists independently of the resident design.

### Documented

- **Documented the limits of the measurement (a hole in the test design).** Because the abort path returns immediately, it skips confirming the 10-second wait, so it was not possible to distinguish "never reclaimed at all" from "reclaimed with delay." Nor was it possible to separate whether the 59 MiB originates from `VDevice` or from the model. Additionally requested only a single line: `grep -E 'CmaTotal|CmaFree' /proc/meminfo`.
- The next design direction is, as in Python, "load and swap models on a single VDevice that lives for the process's lifetime" — but **that too is an inference read from the sister implementation, not a measurement** — the very kind of thing this spec already got wrong once. rev3's first step will be a minimal spike whose sole purpose is to measure whether releasing a model actually reclaims memory. Spec is on the sidecar side, `bb34b57` §12.

## [4.598.5] - 2026-08-08


### Documented

- **The Hailo sidecar's resident design is NO-GO. Cannot proceed until CMA is measured once on real hardware.** The 5.86-second measurement does not change the judgment that "residency is needed," but design review found that the *shape* of the residency mechanism cannot be determined without measuring on real hardware. There is exactly one point of contention — the sidecar creates and discards a `VDevice` on every single inference (`shim.cpp:293, 395, 501, 758`), and the design depends entirely on the assumption that "discarding returns the CMA." However, this repository's own Python implementation, on the same Hailo-10H with the same HailoRT 5.3.0, recorded the opposite (`device_manager_genai.py:95-96`: "CMA is not reclaimed by VDevice.release() within a running session"). For that reason, the Python side never releases the VDevice at all (`device_manager_state.py:58`'s `_maybe_reset_vdevice()` is deliberately a no-op whose body is just a docstring). The spec cited the sister implementation as prior art while failing to carry over its single most important judgment. **The evidence disproving the design was sitting inside the very repository the design cited.**
- What to measure on real hardware: hit `POST /v1/infer/llm/generate` 20 times and trace the trend of `grep CmaFree /proc/meminfo`. If it returns to baseline, the skeleton survives; if it decreases monotonically, the design changes to "share a single VDevice that lives for the process's lifetime." **In addition, if non-reclamation also extends to the sidecar's own release path, the sidecar is already leaking CMA on every single request right now** — this could be a current defect that predates the design question.
- Spec and handoff live on the sidecar repository side (`9c3b652`). 7 remaining review comments carried forward to spec §11.

## [4.598.0] - 2026-08-08

### Changed

- **Made hailo-genai's `GET /v1/models` and `GET /api/runtime` Rust-native.**
  Neither touches the Hailo device; both are complete with just checking HEF file existence and referencing the model table.

```
Rust standalone gap
  remaining work:  52 → 50
    no native path: 31 → 29
```

- **`runtime`'s `context` is always `null`.** This is not an implementation shortcut, but
  **an accurate representation of the fact that the sidecar holds nothing**. The sidecar performs
  `Llm::create` per request and discards it immediately (`yu-hailo-infer`'s
  `router.rs:974-981`), so there is no retained context to report. Python also returns
  `None` when not resident. The test name
  `native_runtime_context_is_null_because_sidecar_retains_nothing` embeds the reason directly,
  so it is not later mistaken for a missing implementation.
- **`/v1/models` returns 200 even with read scope.** `require_admin_scope`
  (`core/web/auth_helpers.py:67-76`) checks **API key scope, not authentication**, and its docstring
  explicitly states that "a session with no API key passes through." Unauthenticated requests are stopped
  separately by middleware (`/ext/hailo-genai` is not in `BYPASS_ROUTES`).
  The reason Python does not apply a scope check only to `/v1/models` is that OpenAI-compatible
  clients need to fetch the listing before hitting `/v1/chat/completions` (admin-only), and this is
  an intentional difference. Pinned down by the test
  `native_v1_models_allows_read_scope_for_openai_client_discovery`.
- The model table reuses the existing `hailo_model_registry::genai_models()`.
  It is built once per process via `OnceCell` (the same shape as Python's one-time import),
  so **no per-request network access occurs**. Making a frozen copy would silently rot when
  the Python-side table changes, so the source is shared.
- The HEF `path` is returned **as configured**, same as Python (if `HAILO_HEF_DIR` is
  relative, it stays relative). Normalizing it would disclose more than Python does — with a relative
  configuration, the full path including the working directory would appear in the response. Do not
  widen disclosure as a side effect of the port.

### Documented

- **The implementer caught 3 instruction errors before starting work** (in this increment alone).
  (1) "Both routes are admin" — `/v1/models` has no scope check;
  (2) "No authorization means it can be hit unauthenticated" — wrong, middleware authenticates separately;
  (3) "`path` is a resolved absolute path" — wrong, it stays relative when configured as relative.
  All three were stopped before entering the code.

## [4.596.0] - 2026-08-07

### Changed

- **Made `POST /api/thumbnails/warmup` Rust-native** (the 2nd of the misc batch).

```
Rust standalone gap
  remaining work:  53 → 52
    no native path: 32 → 31
```

- **The previous standalone stub was a "polite lie."** `files.rs:502-511`, when Python was absent,
  returned not a 503 but a **202 with `{"ok": true, "started": false, "count": N}`**,
  making it look like success while warming nothing at all. A caller looking only at `ok` could not
  tell the difference from real success. Removed by replacing it with a real implementation.
- The core already existed — `resolve_preview_path` (`files.rs:460`) **generates and caches** a cold preview
  (the native `thumbnails_batch` already relies on this). Warmup is reduced to just running that
  in the background.
- Preserved 3 easy-to-drop specification points. **Above 2000 is truncated to the first 2000, not an error**,
  `count` is the count **after filtering** (send 3000, get back 2000), and `started: false` means
  not a failure but that **the same set is already running**.
- Dedup reuses `JobManager`, with the job id as
  `thumbnail-warmup:{hash of the first 100 sorted}`. **The instructions had the implementer build a dedicated
  in-flight set, but the implementer's own judgment was better** — the same semantics are obtained
  without adding new state.
- **The tests cover both sides of dedup.** Submitting the same set twice yields `started: false`, and
  **submitting different sets concurrently yields `started: true` for both**. Since Python dedups per set,
  without the latter case, degeneration of the job id to a constant would go unnoticed
  (the author himself nearly misread it as global). `thumbnails_warmup_populates_preview_cache`
  confirms **that the cache is actually filled** — the sole test that prevents a recurrence of the
  stub silently returning 202 forever.
