## [4.595.0] - 2026-08-07

### Changed

- **Made `GET /api/ai-context` native Rust** (1st of 7 misc items).

```
Rust standalone gap
  remaining work:  54 → 53
    no native path: 33 → 32
```

- **This endpoint is self-description for an AI to trace an instance's capabilities, and if it reports a feature it doesn't actually have, it actively misleads its one and only consumer.** Python pulls `capabilities` from Quart's blueprint registry (`BLUEPRINT_CAPABILITY_MAP`), but since Rust has no equivalent, **it was mapped onto a capability probe instead**. The mapping doesn't follow mechanically, so the judgment calls are stated explicitly.
  - The core 4 (`llm_router`, `image_analysis`, `gateway`, `scheduler`) are always present, since they're always built into yu-server.
  - **`lan_cowork` appears only when its routes are actually mounted.** The LAN Cowork router returns an empty `Router` and 404s when `native_daemon` is disabled, so an unmounted route is not a capability.
  - `hailo` / `wd_tagger` are judged by **"is it configured", never by probing reachability**. Python's `build_ai_context` explicitly states it is "IO-free within this function," and turning a self-description GET into a network probe would be a regression for the endpoint.
- The test `ai_context_matches_python_metadata_and_unmounted_capabilities` pins down that **`lan_cowork` does not appear in capabilities when unmounted**. This is the assertion that guarantees the endpoint doesn't lie. `ai_context_capabilities_follow_actual_configuration` also confirms `hailo` appears when configured and `wd_tagger` is absent when `enabled:false`, showing this isn't a hardcoded list.
- `config_hints` returns only key / severity / message, **never the configuration value itself**. For secret items, only the fact that they are "not configured" is reported.
- `version` caches `VERSION` on first read, and falls back to `"unknown"` if it can't be read. The caching semantics (writing `VERSION` afterward still leaves it at `"unknown"`) are also pinned down by a test.

## [4.594.1] - 2026-08-07

### Fixed

- **`rust_standalone_gap.py` was miscounting the 3 `/sd/*` routes as "not yet ported."** Discovered through actual measurement. `/sd/config`, `/sd/info`, and `/sd/internal/ping` were **already native**, connecting directly to **Stable Diffusion WebUI**, not to Python.
- The cause was that the check **wasn't looking at the destination**. `fwd_get_sd` (`misc_admin.rs:753-766`) pulls the SD base_url from the gateway config via `sd_backend_url(&gw)` (defaulting to SD WebUI's default port `http://127.0.0.1:7860`), and never touches `python_url`. `state.python_client` is just a `reqwest::Client` whose name happens to be confusing — it is not evidence of the destination. Because the function name also starts with `fwd_`, **a name-based check would have been fooled here too**.
- The check was changed to "**whether the URL derives from `python_url`**." All 33 remaining items were audited under the same lens, confirming no other false positives exist. A regression test, `tests/test_rust_standalone_gap.py`, was added.

```
remaining work:  57 → 54
  no native path: 36 → 33
```

- **A measurement tool is never more accurate than its heuristic.** The limitation was documented in the docstring, but **this was the first time it was actually verified against measurement**, and at that point 3 items turned out to be wrong. Rather than papering over it with a patch, the check itself was fixed, and the documented limitation was updated to match the implementation.

### Documented

- A **genuine parity gap** was separately found in the SD gateway (task #42). Python's `_resolve_sd` (`routes/gateway_sd.py:86-99`) honors a per-request `backend_id` (query) and `X-Backend-Id` (header), returning 404 for `not_found` and 400 for `type_mismatch`. Rust's `sd_backend_url` only looks at `defaults.default_sd_backend_id`, so in **multi-backend configurations it always ignores the client's specification and sends to the default**. This is not "not yet ported" but a functional difference, distinct from the reason the tool had originally flagged it (a misjudgment).

## [4.594.0] - 2026-08-07

### Changed

- **comfyui-bridge's Python forwarding has been reduced to zero.** In C3c, `check-workflow-from-file` and `queue-workflow-from-file` were made native Rust, removing the last 2 remaining registrations and completing the work.

```
Rust standalone gap
  remaining work:  61 → 57
    no native path: 40 → 36
comfyui-bridge remaining lines: 0
```

- **This pair has the same shape but opposite error policies.** The first half (the 5-branch sequence of `file_id`(int) → DB lookup → file inspection) is exactly identical, but `check` is **fail-open** — extraction failures, unexpected editor formats, and unforeseen exceptions are all collapsed into a 200 `{"status":"ok"}` so as not to block the user's work. `queue` is fail-closed, distinguishing 422/400/502. **Bundling the error handling together with the shared first half would turn `check` into fail-closed**, so that part was deliberately kept separate, and pinned down with `check_workflow_from_file_fails_open_when_extraction_fails`.
- `migrate_clip_types` is **always applied**, regardless of the truth value of `supplement`. This is to fix stale `clip_type` values on old images (e.g. `"wan"` → `"qwen_image"`) and let re-import through; making it conditional would leave old images broken. This was pinned down using what the mock actually received.
- The new implementation consists of 4 helpers (`check_model_nodes`, `extract_gen_params_from_image`, `supplement_model_nodes`, `migrate_clip_types`). **This is the only step in this group where no existing Rust implementation existed at all.** The `POST /prompt` call to ComfyUI and the id lookup on `files.path` reused existing code.

### Removed

- **Removed the registrations for `POST /api/custom-nodes` and `GET /api/model-registry/{id}`.** These had initially been counted as "2 unported items," but they turned out to be **methods that don't exist on the Python side** — Python only provides `GET /api/custom-nodes`, `GET,POST /api/model-registry`, and `DELETE /api/model-registry/<entry_id>`, 4 in total (`comfyui_discovery_api.py:68`, `comfyui_api_model_registry_routes.py:120,150,185`). There were also zero calls from the UI. Forwarding them would just have Python return 405 anyway, so **removal, not porting, was the correct finish**. axum now returns 405 on its own, eliminating the round trip.
- The comment "Python-proxied complex routes (not yet migrated)" was no longer accurate, and was replaced.

### Documented

- **Measuring reachability before porting changed the work — this happened 3 times in this group.** (1) In C1, a full-path grep almost misjudged 6 live routes as having "zero calls" (because the UI builds URLs dynamically); (2) in C3a, an unreachable branch had been instructed to be pinned down by a test; (3) in C3c, the "2 items that should be ported" turned out to be deletion targets. In each case this was caught before work began.
- `proxy_generic` was left in place with zero calls (whether to remove it is left for a separate decision).
- **Every porting step in this group revealed the shape of "just building on top of an existing piece"** — custom-nodes had 6 siblings already native, model-registry already had native POST/DELETE, checkpoint-info had path-containment pieces on both sides, and extract-workflow had PNG/EXIF/comfyui detection already in `meta-extract`. C3c was the sole exception, the only step that truly required new implementation.

## [4.593.0] - 2026-08-07

### Changed

- **comfyui-bridge C3b: made `POST /api/upload-controlnet-image` native Rust.** The 8th of 10 comfyui-bridge routes.

```
Rust standalone gap
  remaining work:  62 → 61
    no native path: 41 → 40
```

- The first half (the multipart `image` part, extension validation, bounded read) is identical to C3a's `extract-workflow`, so it was factored out as `read_image_upload`. However, **the default filename differs** (`extract-workflow` uses `unknown.png`, this one uses `controlnet_input.png`), so that part was kept separate.
- **The extension is decided not by "the uploaded filename" but by "sniffing the byte sequence."** `_detect_image_format` (`comfyui_client_upload.py:16-21`) treats a leading `FF D8` as jpg, `RIFF....WEBP` as webp, and **everything else as png**, then reattaches that extension to the filename's stem before sending. ⟹ Sending JPEG bytes under a filename like `x.png` results in it being stored as `x.jpg`. Because ComfyUI's behavior varies by stored filename, this is **intentional specification**, and it was pinned down with `upload_controlnet_image_sniffs_jpeg_under_png_filename`. Matching Python, anything that is neither JPEG nor WEBP is not validated and treated as png (no validation was added beyond what Python has).
- The fallback of **returning the sent filename** when ComfyUI's response JSON lacks a `name` was also preserved.
- Upstream failures return **502** (not 500). ComfyUI is an upstream service, hence bad gateway.

## [4.592.0] - 2026-08-07

### Fixed

- **EXIF `UserComment` was being written by the app itself, yet the app couldn't read its own writes back.** `read_exif_tags` (`meta-extract/src/exif_reader.rs`) stringified every field via `display_value()`, but EXIF's `Undefined` type renders under that as **`0x<hex>`**. Meanwhile this very app writes UserComment as `b"UNICODE\x00"` plus UTF-16 in `core/bridge_core/bridge_save.py:33-50`, with a comment explicitly stating it's written "so that a metadata parser can read it." ⟹ Neither `YU_META:` detection nor JSON parsing could ever succeed, and the value that `tagdb-core/src/import/fallback_chain.rs:81-100` passed as `exif:UserComment` was **always unparseable**. The `exif:UserComment` key list held in `comfyui.rs` could never match.
- For `Tag::UserComment` only, the `UNICODE\0` / `ASCII\0\0\0` prefix is now stripped before decoding. **Since this changes the output of a shared function, its consumers were checked** — `read_exif_tags` is called only from two places, `tagdb-core`'s import fallback and `yu-server/routes/misc_admin.rs`, and in both cases the decoded output is correct. This was pinned down with 4 tests, including a round-trip test that builds input the same way `bridge_save.py` does (UNICODE / ASCII / no prefix / truncated UTF-16 bytes).

### Changed

- **comfyui-bridge C3a: made `parse-workflow-params` and `extract-workflow` native Rust.**

```
Rust standalone gap
  remaining work:  64 → 62
    no native path: 43 → 41
```

- Image metadata parsing used what **already existed** in `crates/meta-extract` (tEXt/iTXt in `png.rs`, `exif_reader.rs`, workflow detection in `comfyui.rs`). Nothing was reimplemented. Only `extract_simple_params` is new — `simple_builder.rs`'s `parse_params`/`build_workflow` run in the **opposite direction** (parameters → workflow) and couldn't be reused.
- For EXIF, a `Cursor<&[u8]>` entry point was added instead of creating a temp file (also avoiding path leakage).
- **Compressed iTXt is distinguished with a dedicated 422 message** — `png.rs` doesn't support compressed iTXt, but Python's PIL can read it, so porting as-is would mean **a PNG that can be extracted today would become "no metadata" after porting**. Rather than folding it into the generic `ok:false`, it returns `Compressed iTXt workflow metadata is not supported`.

### Documented

- **A spec error was caught by the implementer before starting (the 11th such catch overall).** It had initially been written as "unsupported extension → 422," but in fact `validate_image_filename` runs first, so it's **400**. Moreover, the `"Unsupported format"` branch in `extract_workflow_from_image` is **unreachable from this route**, since `_ALLOWED_IMAGE_EXTS = {"png","jpg","jpeg","webp"}` is an **exact match** to the corresponding set — and there had been an instruction to **pin down unreachable paths with a test**. The 422 that actually occurs is for "a supported extension but no workflow metadata." The original text was left in plan §6.3, with a dated correction appended below it.

## [4.589.0] - 2026-08-07

### Added

- **`scripts/rust_standalone_gap.py`** —— enumerates the routes that forward to
  Python, and expresses the remaining porting work as a single number.
  **It reaches 0 when the port is complete.** It was newly created because the
  existing metrics could not reveal how much work remained.
  `rust_migration_coverage.py` itself warns in its own docstring that
  "**routes that merely forward are also counted as 'covered'**", and its 98.8%
  is a confirmation that the route exists, not a confirmation that it works.
- **`scripts/rust_proxy_keep.txt`** —— a registry of deliberate decisions to
  keep certain routes forwarding. Same prefix-match, `#`-comment format as
  `mcp_parity_exceptions.txt`. **Each entry is required to state a reason and
  cite the decision document it comes from** —— an entry without grounds would
  quietly erase remaining work, so anything that cannot be justified in writing
  is not listed (the correct default is for it to show up as remaining work
  when it cannot be listed).

```
Rust standalone gap
  total routes:            881
  forward to Python:       79
    deliberate proxy-keep: 12
    remaining work:        67
      no native path:      46
      native + fallback:   6
      unclassified:        15
```

- **Split the forwards into "no native path exists at all" and "native path
  with a conditional fallback."** Without this split, work items that differ
  by orders of magnitude end up listed side by side. Example:
  `/api/thumbnail/{file_id}` only falls back to Python when the DB path
  contains `!` (a member inside an archive); ordinary files are native.
  `/ext/hailo-genai/api/llm/generate` has no native path at all. Cases that
  cannot be determined are left as `unclassified` rather than guessed at (a
  checkable "unknown" is worth more than a confident misclassification).

### Documented

- **Made explicit that the three metrics have different denominators.**
  Conflating them is the main cause of "we don't know what's left."
  - MCP-exposed-path basis: 505/511 = 98.8% (`rust_migration_coverage.py`)
  - Python route-registration basis: 388/438 = 88.6%
    (`rust-migration-inventory.yaml`)
  - Rust forward measurement: 814/881 = 92.4% (this increment)
- **The `status` field in `rust-migration-inventory.yaml` is hand-maintained
  and preserved across regeneration, so it goes stale.** Actual measurement
  showed that all 6 page routes marked `proxied`
  (`/agent_memory`, `/crypto_tools`, `/lan_cowork`, `/llm_router`,
  `/mesh_inference`, `/sw.js`) were **already Rust-native**
  (the `frontend::*` at `main.rs:2223, 2251-2255`).
- Confirmed the current state of Hailo through actual measurement.
  **Inference is both split out and ported to Rust** (depends on
  `eauesque/yu-hailo-infer` pinned to a git rev; `infer_client.rs` calls
  `/v1/infer/*`; `crates/yu-infer` is only a shim that produces the sidecar
  binary for the same target), and **the screen is also served by Rust**
  (the `page!` in `frontend.rs:97-102` renders the extension's Jinja template
  via minijinja). What remains is only the 26 API routes under
  `/ext/hailo-genai` and `/ext/hailo-yolo`. Of these, `vlm/generate` and
  `chat/send` already use the infer client, and only fall back to Python when
  there is an image attachment, web_search, or subprocess mode.

## [4.588.2] - 2026-08-07

### Fixed

- **Partial import failures were being reported as success.** Even when some
  of the N files a peer presented failed to transfer, the session was
  recorded with `status="completed"` and `last_seen_rowid=max_rowid`, and the
  UI overwrote the count to `done/done` upon completion. Three symptoms were
  compounding each other.
  - `batch_zip` unconditionally returns `Ok(())` at the end
    (`lan_cowork_import_executor.rs:351`). A chunk download failure falls
    back to `individual_http`, and a failure there too just leaves a
    `tracing::warn!` and moves on to the next one — it is never registered
    into `import_file_id_map`. The caller had no way to distinguish this from
    success.
  - **The cursor was skipping past files that had never been fetched.** The
    next diff-mode run requires `after_rowid=last_seen_rowid`, so a failed
    file is never presented again. However, the UI creates a new session
    every time, and `create_session` sets `last_seen_rowid=NULL`
    (`lan_cowork_import_state.rs:186`), so on the UI path the cursor was
    write-only. It was only reachable by calling `POST /execute` directly
    with an existing `session_id`.
  - **The UI was erasing the failure count (and this one had real impact).**
    `import-panel.ts:97` discards `total_files` by writing
    `` `${s.done_files} / ${s.done_files}` ``, so even if the previous poll
    had shown `40 / 100`, on completion it was overwritten to **`40 / 40`**
    and `Import completed` was displayed. Since this is an overwrite rather
    than an omission, the user had no way to notice the failure. Task #19 had
    recorded this as a "latent defect," but that assessment only looked at
    the cursor symptom — this symptom occurs on the ordinary UI path.
- The fix counts, after the transfer, how many of `to_import` are absent from
  `import_file_id_map`, and **writes `last_seen_rowid` only when that count is
  0.** When it is not 0, only `status="completed"` is written and the cursor
  is left untouched. Items whose metadata was corrupted and so were never
  transferred are also (deliberately) counted as unprocessed.
- **A watermark approach (advance to the smallest failed rowid minus 1) was
  not taken.** `max_rowid` is an upper bound on the snapshot, and no mapping
  from "remote file id → rowid" exists anywhere in this code; an incorrect
  watermark would silently lose data. Not advancing only results in
  redundant re-presentation —— **waste beats loss.**
- **`status` was left as `"completed"`.** Setting it to `"failed"` would make
  the UI hide progress and show an error instead
  (`import-panel.ts:103-107`), which would be wrong for a run that succeeded
  on 99 of 100 files. No new status value was added either —— `done_files` is
  incremented for both `"done"` and `"skipped"`
  (`import_state.rs:320-326`), so the gap against `total_files` **exactly
  matches the count of transfer failures**, making it possible to detect a
  partial failure without touching either the schema or the status
  vocabulary.
- **Python had the exact same shape of defect, and it was fixed at the same
  time** (`import_executor.py:159-164`). Since this gap was common to both
  implementations, and the fix constitutes a behavior change (same precedent
  as `/fleet/logs/stream`).
- The UI now retains `done / total`, does not fill the progress bar to 100%
  when `done < total`, and shows the `lan_cowork.import.partial`
  notification. Keys were added to 22 files across 11 languages.

## [4.588.1] - 2026-08-07

### Fixed

- **Removed 6 test-only seams from the production build.** Created a new
  `test-seams` feature for `lan-cowork`, and gated
  `TEST_ALLOW_LOOPBACK`, `TEST_DESCRIPTOR`, `TEST_LOCK`, `test_guard`, and
  `reset_client_state` (`lan_cowork_descriptor.rs`), along with the 2 branches
  on the production side that read them (the loopback exception in
  `is_reachable_peer_ip`, and the override check in
  `descriptor_for_handler`), behind
  `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-seams"))]`. Because the crate is published
  standalone, previously **any downstream crate that depended on it could
  disable the loopback guard.** yu-server only enables the feature from
  `[dev-dependencies]` (since the workspace uses `resolver = "2"`, it does not
  merge into non-test builds).
- **While fixing this, found 2 more seams of the same shape and gated them the
  same way.** `PeerRegistry::insert_for_test`
  (`lan_cowork_registry.rs:97`) writes an arbitrary `PeerInfo` into the
  trusted registry without going through the DB or validation, which is
  heavier than the two descriptor seams (it forges peer identity).
  `sign_headers` (`auth/peer_transport.rs:539`) takes the seed as an argument,
  so it is not a privilege escalation but an exposed-surface-area issue.
- **`cargo tree` proves nothing, so the fix was verified with a sentinel.**
  Unless `--no-dev-dependencies` is passed, `cargo tree` always renders dev
  edges, making a correct state and a leaking state look identical. A
  `#[cfg(feature = "test-seams")] compile_error!` was placed temporarily in
  `lib.rs`, and it was confirmed that `cargo build -p yu-server` succeeds
  while `cargo test -p yu-server` fails on that compile_error (and, after
  removing it, that the build succeeds again). If the feature were leaking
  into production, the build side would fail, which rules out "it just looks
  fixed."
- **Made `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (31 findings).**
  The CI in the extraction-destination repo had been **failing at this exact
  step** since its first commit (Format passed, Test never even ran). The
  main repo had never once run clippy on this crate, so it had gone through
  unnoticed. There were zero actual bugs; the breakdown was unused imports,
  dead code, and style. `#[allow]` was scoped as narrowly as possible, and
  every instance carries a reason comment.
- **`gpu_info` was duplicating the same selection logic instead of calling
  `gpu_info_from`** (`lan_cowork_fleet_machine.rs`). The dead_code warning was
  a consequence of that duplication; sealing it with `#[cfg(test)]` would
  have **frozen in place a state where the test verifies the duplicate rather
  than the production path.** Changed it to delegate instead.
  `gpu_windows_wmi` needs to be called only when the probe fails, so it was
  kept as `impl FnOnce` to preserve lazy evaluation (passing it as an argument
  would run WMI every time).

### Changed

- Made the extraction-destination repo's sync script compare `[features]` as
  well. Previously it only looked at the set of dependency names, so
  **an added feature went undetected** —— `src/` is copied verbatim, so even
  if `#[cfg(feature = "x")]` arrives, the mirror silently generates nothing
  for it. Also added `docs/SECURITY_REVIEW.md` (a copy of the parent's
  `LAN_COWORK_SECURITY_REVIEW.md`) to the copy targets, since it lives outside
  the crate and had been missed.
- Found and fixed a broken section-parsing bug in that same script through
  actual measurement. Because awk processes `-v` value escaping first,
  `'^\[features\]'` degenerated into the character class `'^[features]'`,
  which ended up picking up keys from `[package]` as well. **Because it exits
  non-zero, this looked at a glance like it was "correctly detecting drift."**
  Changed it to an exact-match comparison, and added a check that aborts as a
  parse failure if the dependency count parses to 0.

## [4.588.0] - 2026-08-07

### Changed

- **Made `lan-cowork` hold its own parity verification vectors, so that
  `cargo test` passes for the crate standalone.** This was the last obstacle
  to extraction. Moved the 8 files under `tests/vectors/` to
  `crates/lan-cowork/tests/vectors/`, and aligned the 9 `include_str!` sites
  and the output destinations of the 7 generators.
- **This was a coupling that did not show up in `Cargo.toml`.** Measured it
  by copying `crates/lan-cowork/{src,migrations}` outside the workspace:
  `cargo build` succeeded, but `cargo test` failed with 9 errors ——
  `include_str!` resolves **relative to the source file**, and it was
  reaching up four directory levels to the repo root. "Zero path
  dependencies," established in the previous increment, **was not proof of
  independence.** ⟹ Proving an extraction is actually independent requires
  building it outside for real, nothing less.
- **Overturned decision (4), "leave the vectors in the main repo," from S4
  design §3.10.** The implementer stopped before starting, reported it, and
  obtained a ruling from design-advisor. The grounds were not analogy but two
  actual measurements —— (a) the 8 JSON files are read only from the 9 sites
  in `crates/lan-cowork/src`; none of the Python tests, `parity_harness.py`,
  `verify_rust_compat`, or `pre_push_check.py` read them, meaning **there are
  zero consumers on the main-repo side**; (b) the live parity contract is
  `parity_harness.py` (281 PASS acceptance conditions), not the vectors, so
  decision (4)'s sole affirmative argument — "the vectors are the parity
  contract itself" — was contrary to fact. In addition, following (4) would
  make up to 15 cryptography internals `pub`, which **contradicts decision (2)
  in the same document** (which rejected a test-only feature on the grounds
  that it "widens the public surface of a crate reviewed in isolation"). The
  original decision text was not deleted; a dated revision section was
  appended below it, and among decision (5)'s three grounds, "cannot depend on
  an unpublished private crate" was noted as **not transferable here** (the
  JSON can simply be copied).
- Measured the safety of the placement by comparing `cargo metadata
  --no-deps` before and after. `lan-cowork`'s targets are a single `lib`
  both before and after, with no increase in integration-test targets (this
  was measured, not inferred from the spec).

### Added

- Added **§3.7** to the security review document. Of the 4 test-only seams in
  `lan_cowork_descriptor.rs:145-164`, 2 are only `pub` + `#[doc(hidden)]` and
  **lack `#[cfg(test)]`.** `#[doc(hidden)]` only hides an item from rustdoc
  and has no effect on visibility, so **any code that depends on this crate
  can call them.** `TEST_ALLOW_LOOPBACK` can disable production's
  `is_reachable_peer_ip` loopback guard, and `TEST_DESCRIPTOR` can wholesale
  replace production's `descriptor_for_handler` descriptor resolution (the
  wider bypass surface of the two). `test_guard` and `reset_client_state` in
  the same block have the same shape but a different nature (they undo a
  bypass rather than execute one). Only 1 consumer in the entire workspace
  requires `pub`. **Not fixed in this increment, recorded only** —— once the
  test layout is settled in S4e, it can be narrowed to `pub(crate)`.

Verification: lan-cowork **509 passed / 0 failed** (same count as before the
move), yu-server 989 passed / 12 failed (known baseline),
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets` clean,
`grep 'include_str!("../../..'` 0 hits, generator round-trips byte-identical,
pre_push exit 0.

  `tagdb-core = { path = "../tagdb-core" }`, and moved
  `apply_lan_cowork_standalone_schema` and
  `086_lan_cowork_peer_family.sql` into
  `crates/lan-cowork/{src/schema.rs, migrations/}`. The return type changed
  from `TagdbError` to `sqlx::Error`. The tagdb-core-side idempotency test was
  moved along with it.
- **Decided by measurement.** `cargo check -p lan-cowork` (lib only) passed
  without tagdb-core, while `--all-targets` alone produced 14 errors ——
  meaning it was **a test-only dependency.**
- **Overturned decision (5), "leave the schema in tagdb-core," from S4 design
  §3.10.** The original decision text was not deleted; a dated revision
  section was appended below it. Three reasons —— (a) (5)'s stated grounds,
  "duplication of migration-ordering management," do not apply, because 086
  is not on the ordering sequence (what's enumerated there are `Migration`
  entries in the 084/085 style; 086 is only referenced once, from the
  standalone function); (b) (5)'s own warning that "after the split, the peer
  token and pairing request table definitions would sit in a separate repo —
  **exactly what a security review is supposed to examine**" has now, with
  the split actually happening, turned into a reason to move it; (c)
  tagdb-core is an unpublished private repo, so the extraction destination
  cannot depend on it, and leaving it behind would mean **not a single test
  runs at the destination.**
- Added **§3.5, "`8.8.8.8` is a discovery target, not a communication
  target,"** to the security review document. `UdpSocket::connect` merely
  sets a default destination and sends no packet; its purpose is to determine
  the outbound route via `local_addr()`. Recorded this preemptively because it
  is easy for a review of the public repo to flag it incorrectly (also noting
  that if it were ever changed to `TcpStream`, that would be an actual
  connection and would deserve flagging).

  md files, and by gitignore's **last-match-wins** rule, silently canceled out

in), tagdb-core 51 passed, yu-server 989 passed / 12 failed (matches known
baseline), `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` clean, `path =` 0 hits,

## [4.586.1] - 2026-08-06

### Fixed

- **Fixed a false FAILED report on fleet restart.** Because a Rust peer can restart via `execv` faster than the first poll (after 3 seconds), the conjunction `saw_down && uptime < pre_uptime` alone would **misreport a successful restart as `restart_timeout` after 60 seconds**, triggering a restart loop across the whole fleet. Added `uptime < elapsed_since_t0` as a disjunct. Since `uptime` is process lifetime (`state.start_time.elapsed()`) and resets to 0 on `execv`, when there is no restart, `uptime = pre_uptime + elapsed ≥ elapsed`, so the condition does not hold. **This is one-directional and never turns a true FAILED into a false SUCCESS.** The Python side was left unchanged (its own restart is slow enough that `saw_down` reliably holds) — this is a **deliberate parity deviation**, documented in `lan_cowork_fleet_dispatch.rs:810-877`.
- **During implementation, a false-SUCCESS path was introduced once and then removed.** An initial version added a 2.0-second epsilon, but for the non-restart case, `elapsed` cancels out of `pre_uptime + elapsed < elapsed + 2.0 ⟺ pre_uptime < 2`, leaving a state where **a peer with less than 2 seconds of uptime would be reported as permanently successful**. Nodes in a boot loop are exactly the ones with small `pre_uptime`, so the very case we most want to detect would slip through. The rationale for the epsilon (truncation, polling-interval delay) both push the reported value smaller, which only makes detection easier — there was nothing to gain. Added a regression test centered on `pre_uptime ∈ {0,1}` and confirmed by measurement that it fails if the epsilon is reintroduced.

### Added

- `docs/development/development_docs/LAN_COWORK_SECURITY_REVIEW.md` — a security review guide for the point of separation into an independent repo. Contains only things that cannot be known without reading outside the crate (authorization takes effect in the route body, not the declaration; `require_admin_scope` is fail-open; the nonce allowlist is also fail-open; the static salt is safe only because the token is 256 bits; etc.).

## [4.586.0] - 2026-08-06

### Fixed

- **Added a per-IP connection limit on `/ext/lan_cowork/fleet/logs/stream` (both Python and Rust).** This was not a Rust regression but **a gap common to both implementations** — Python streamed `iter_sse_events(log_ring, ...)` directly, and in Rust, `local_log_response` was not calling `register_connection`. Both implementations already enforce a limit on the core-side log SSE (3 per IP in both), so fixing only one side would break parity. Limit is **3**; exceeding it returns **429** plus `{"error": "too_many_log_sse_connections"}`. Release is via a `Drop` guard in Rust and `try/finally` in Python. The relay branch does not consume local resources, so it was deliberately left unlimited.
- The guard initially held a **strong `Arc<dyn LanCoworkHost>`**, keeping `AppState` alive and breaking an existing test that observes `RecvError::Closed` on `Arc` drop. Changed to `Weak` plus `.upgrade()`. **The guard meant to release a resource was itself holding on to a different resource.**

Since `path_is_within`'s own doc comment states "this is only half of the comparison; unless resolution is done first, the containment check silently fails," it must not be split across a crate seam. `arch-constraints.yaml:182` needs no update (the location and meaning of the shared predicate are unchanged). <br>

## [4.581.0] - 2026-08-06

### Changed

- **S4b — moved authorization behind the host trait. The riskiest step of the split.** Eliminated every reference from LAN Cowork production code to `crate::auth::scope::{require_session, AuthContext}` and `crate::auth::client_ip::ClientIp` (down to zero remaining). <br>
  `async fn require_session(&self, session: Option<&Session>) -> Option<Response>`. **All five properties that had to be preserved were preserved** — (1) async, (2) the permit path for `pin_auth_enabled == false`, (3) not collapsing `Option<&Session>`, (4) 401 plus a fixed body, and (5) **not reading `AuthContext.reason`**. <br>
  (5) was something the review surfaced and was absent from design-document rev1 — because the auth chain evaluates the API key before the session, branching on `reason` would **wrongly reject a request that presented both a valid session and an unrelated API key**. Because `AuthContext` was in view for this increment, it existed as a **structural temptation**. <br>
  The implementation is a **thin delegation, not a reimplementation** — leaving no room for meaning to drift. <br>
  `ClientIp` became `PeerSourceIp(pub String)`. **It is not projected down to `IpAddr`** — because `"unknown"` is used as the rate-limit bucket key, a DB column, and in the request↔IP binding check, projecting it would break one of these. The insertion point is on the core side (`auth/middleware.rs:84`). <br>
  Full suite: 1491 passed / 13 failed, an identical set to before.

(2) Wrapped `agent_journal::record_action` in a trait method `record_journal_action`, cutting off `lan_cowork.rs`'s direct import. (3) Replaced `security::CspNonce` with a **neutral newtype owned by LAN Cowork, `FleetUiNonce`**, arranged so that core's `security::layer` inserts it. (4) Flattened the intra-doc link at `peer_pairing_crypto.rs:102` into plain text (since it would become unresolvable once it crosses the crate boundary). <br>
  **Why the neutral newtype was chosen over the other option for `CspNonce`** — the alternative (defining an extractor on the LAN Cowork side) would still need to read `crate::security::CspNonce` internally, so it **merely moves the reference to a different file** without eliminating it. With a neutral newtype, the reference stays on the core side, which also matches the post-split dependency direction (core → LAN Cowork). <br>
  Measured: production dependencies went from **17 kinds across 32 sites to 16 kinds across 28 sites**. The one remaining `crate::sse` reference is a legitimate holdover inside `lan_cowork_host.rs`'s impl, where an `SseEvent` is actually constructed; the one remaining `agent_journal` reference is likewise a deliberate seam via delegation to the trait impl. <br>
  Full suite: 1491 passed / 13 failed, an identical set to before.

### Fixed

- **Recorded a third flaw in the measurement method** — because the scanning script reads the source with a regular expression, **it counts a fully-qualified path inside a doc comment as an actual reference.** Observed during the S4a implementation — where `RelayedSseEvent`'s doc comment wrote `crate::sse::SseEvent`, it was counted as one reference even though the import and the type itself were already gone. <br>
  This brings the known blind spots to three — (i) re-exports (where `lan_cowork` does not appear in the path name), (ii) coupling not expressed as `crate::` notation (`include_str!`, external crates), and (iii) failure to distinguish comments from real code. **Documented explicitly in the design document §1.0.**

## [4.576.0] - 2026-08-05

### Changed

- **S3c — neutralized the log delivery path.** Added `log_open(limit, level)` to the trait, bringing it to **fifteen methods**.
  Introduced a LAN Cowork-owned neutral type `LogLine` (five fields: seq/timestamp/level/target/message) and
  `LogEvent { Line, Closed }`, and pushed out core's `LogRingBuffer`/`LogEntry` from the production path in
  `lan_cowork_fleet_ops.rs`.<br>
  **Avoided three traps** (any one of which, alone, could cause "compiles and tests pass, but behavior silently changes"):<br>
  (1) **level vocabulary** — core uses `WARN`, the API uses `WARNING`. If the normalized name is put onto
  `LogLine.level`, `TRACE`'s rank shifts from 0→1, and **a line that should be dropped today passes through** on a
  `level=DEBUG` request. Conversely, if the API vocabulary is passed to `log_open`, `ring.recent` drops the unknown
  term to rank 0, and **backlog filtering silently disappears**. ⇒ Both the entry and exit were pinned to core
  vocabulary, and the `WARNING→WARN` mapping plus live filtering were kept on the LAN Cowork side.<br>
  (2) **Not splitting `subscribe` and `recent` into two methods** — writing the order reversed still compiles and
  still passes tests, only rarely dropping a single log line.<br>
  (3) **The distinction between `Lagged`/`Closed`** — since these vanish under `BoxStream<LogLine>`, a `LogEvent`
  enum was introduced instead.<br>
  **Demonstrated that the ordering guarantee is actually gripped by the tests** — a mutation swapping `subscribe`
  and `recent` inside the impl causes
  `log_sse_live_filter_seam_close_and_connection_budget_are_pinned` to fail. **And it fails for the right reason** —
  with the order reversed, the injected line occurs after the backlog snapshot but before `subscribe`, so
  **it appears in neither the backlog nor the live stream**.
  `seam_hook` was also relocated into the impl side (leaving it at its old location would make it unreachable).<br>
  Full suite: 1492 passed / 13 failed, the same set as before.

### Fixed

- **Fixed a defect where the `wd_tagger` test failed about half the time** (discovered during S3b verification).
  ```rust
  assert_eq!(elapsed * 100.0, (elapsed * 100.0).round());
  ```
  Since `elapsed` is a **measured wall-clock time**, it differs every run, and even a value correctly rounded to
  two decimal places can fail this assertion —
  `4.27 * 100.0 == 426.99999999999994`, `4.89 → 488.99999999999994`,
  `4.44 → 444.00000000000006`. Six standalone runs measured **three passes / three failures**.<br>
  **This was eating away at the verification of the increment itself** — the judgment of "same set as the existing
  13 failures" fluctuated independently of the increment's content, making it **impossible to distinguish
  regression from chance**. In fact, during S3b's verification, this was once suspected to be "S3b broke
  something," and after seeing two isolated failures, near-certainty had set in.<br>
  Changed to an epsilon comparison (`< 1e-6`), and **demonstrated it was not loosened too far** —
  removing the rounding on the production side triggers the assertion all five times (`got 4.798488`, etc.).
  Also confirmed eight consecutive passes.
  No defect of the same shape exists elsewhere (scanned all `.rs` files).

## [4.574.0] - 2026-08-05

### Changed

- **S3a — the first step in decoupling the LAN Cowork handlers from `SharedState`.**
  **Removed the `Clone` supertrait** from `LanCoworkHost` (`Clone: Sized` was blocking trait-object conversion —
  a leftover from an abandoned generic-based design), and moved the implementation from `SharedState` to
  **`AppState`**. Introduced `LanCoworkState` (= `Arc<dyn LanCoworkHost>` plus three LAN Cowork-owned `Arc`s), and
  converted `lan_cowork_fleet_ui.rs` to extract that one route as `Router<LanCoworkState>`.
  Added `render_nav` to the trait, **hiding the `minijinja` type from LAN Cowork**.
  `chief_enabled` now takes `&dyn LanCoworkHost`.<br>
  **The design doc went through four rounds of rejection, resolving 19 must-fix items before implementation
  began** (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-05-lan-cowork-s3-handler-decoupling.md`). Its core claim, "the trait is
  object-safe," was **false** — every piece of evidence cited (all methods synchronous, `&self`, no `Self`
  return) was individually true, yet the blocker was in the supertrait one line above, so
  **the evidence did not actually support the conclusion**.<br>
  **`AppState`'s three fields were made per-field `Arc`s, without renaming them** (the existing 135 call sites
  pass through via `Deref`). ⚠ **Duplicating them breaks things silently** — a duplicated `peer_registry`'s
  `OnceLock` never receives `main.rs`'s `set()` call, so **the route is permanently 503**; a duplicated
  `settings_lock` splits the mutex that serializes `config.json`'s read-modify-write, and
  **allowlist updates, consent responses, and peer revocation are occasionally lost**. Both **compile and pass
  tests**.<br>
  **Demonstrated discriminating power** — consolidated construction into a single `LanCoworkState::from_shared()`
  (the only struct-literal construction site inside the crate), then mutated inside it and confirmed the identity
  test and 5/9 of the `fleet_ui` tests fail.<br>
  **The `Arc::ptr_eq` check added initially guarded nothing** — since the test itself calls `Arc::clone` to
  construct the value and then asserts its own identity, **the very defect it was meant to catch (`main.rs`
  changed to `Arc::new`) could occur and it would still keep passing**. ⟹ Changed the test to go through the same
  seam as production. "It failed when mutated" **does not constitute proof unless you also ask what was
  mutated**.<br>

## [4.566.0] - 2026-08-05

### Added

- As F4a-1a of the LAN Cowork fleet management port, moved the Python `FleetManager` to Rust. The restartable manager owned by `AppState` uses the native registry and the persistent chief configuration as explicit gates, starting and stopping both after boot and at runtime OFF/ON. Polling uses `build_peer_client` and nonce-bearing `build_peer_headers_at`, fixes `X-Requested-With: FleetManager`, and sends even to peers without a token. Ported the cache/consecutive-failure-count pruning, soft-prune, 5-second timeout, node-wide 10-peer semaphore, and the `PeerRegistry::update_telemetry` write-back, without holding the cache lock across an await.<br>**Drop the nonce and all four functions silently become 401** —— `/ext/lan_cowork/fleet/` is included in `NONCE_REQUIRED_PREFIXES`, and since 401 becomes `http_401` and falls under the snapshot's concealment condition, "the list is always empty because every peer returns 401" holds without producing a single error. Therefore use `build_peer_headers_at`, not `make_signature_headers` (which returns only `X-Peer-Ts` and `X-Peer-Sig`).<br>**Do not add a token check to polling** —— Python sends even to peers without a token, gets a 401, and hides it. Adding a check would mean `last_error` no longer starts with `http_4`, and the concealment would **invert**: unpaired peers' names would appear in the fleet list.<br>Demonstrated discriminative power with six mutation controls (nonce removal, `X-Requested-With` defaulting, dropping `info` from the concealment condition, deletion of prune on refresh, removal of the semaphore, removal of counter reset on success). **All six controls failed as expected** (baseline: 11 passed).<br>Note also that the sandbox to which the implementation was delegated does not permit loopback binding (`Operation not permitted`), so mock HTTP tests could not be run there; this was separately verified during this session by other means. **Do not misdiagnose "unable to run" as "the tests are weak" and relax the bar.**

## [4.565.0] - 2026-08-05

### Added

- Ported LAN Cowork's `my-permissions` to Rust (second stage of the repo-separation roadmap). **Authorization uses only `session_guard` → `require_session`** —— `require_admin_scope` **fails OPEN** against LAN Cowork's bypass route (`auth/scope.rs:41` returns `_ => return None`; `middleware.rs:195` sets `reason = "lan_cowork_fleet_peer"`). Using it would **open every LAN peer's permission list to any admin-scope API key holder**. Because the auth chain evaluates the API key before the session, any judgment based on `AuthContext.reason` would be wrong across the board. `require_session` reads `tower_sessions::Session` directly.<br>**The order is reversed relative to the fleet routes** —— the session check precedes the `peer_registry` check, and no session plus LAN Cowork disabled is **401** (not 503).<br>**Sending goes through `build_peer_client`** (rejects public IPs and link-local addresses, pins the resolved IP, disallows redirects). **`PeerTransport::send` is not used** — only the signature-header generation is borrowed from it —— because `send` calls `invalidate_outbound_token` on a 401, so **a single 401 would self-destruct the pairing**.<br>Cache TTL is monotonic (`Instant`); token-expiry judgment is wall-clock (`unix_now`). Mixing the two up breaks the expiry judgment. The 10-peer concurrency semaphore is **shared across the whole process** (do not create one per request). HTTP always returns 200; a peer's individual failure is expressed via `peers[].error` and `null` (not `false`) in the four permission fields.<br>Demonstrated discriminative power with seven mutation controls (session guard always-fail / always-succeed, swapping in `require_admin_scope`, removal of self-filtering, removal of the outer timeout, cache invalidation, collapsing the 409 mapping). **All seven controls failed as expected.** Note that `connection_failure_is_unreachable_not_timeout` pins a constant and thus has no discriminative power; the true grip on the outer timeout lies in `slow_response_maps_to_timeout` (a four-second delay against the client's ten-second timeout).

### Fixed

- Fixed the problem where **`batch_zip`'s tests asserted the old contract and kept failing on main**. Although 8dfcba132 hardened `inspect_zip` so that **a zip containing a remote id outside the request is rejected archive-wide** (any other anomaly in the same loop is likewise rejected wholesale), the tests still asserted the old, lenient contract of "only skip reading the entries outside the request." Rewrote the tests to match the new contract, asserting that 999 is never persisted, that 3 enters via the fallback to individual_http, and that the request splits into two: zip plus individual. This was missed because **`pre_push_check.py` does not run `cargo test`** (main still has 13 red tests even after this increment applies; tracked separately).

## [4.564.0] - 2026-08-05

### Added

- Sixth stage of the LAN Cowork fleet group port (F3c2). Ported `/fleet/update` to Rust, **completing the port of all 23 fleet routes**. **This is the largest and most destructive increment among the fleet routes** (it rewrites its own code via git pull, then self-replaces the process). The design received one design-advisor ruling and reflected its 4 must-fix items.<br>**The only difference from F3c1 (`restart`) is a single point** —— `check_update_allowed(.., allow_consent=true, include_restart_allowlist=**false**)`. Since Python does not pass that argument (defaulting to false), **a peer that exists only in `allow_restart_from` cannot be updated**. Copying F3c1's call pattern would loosen the authorization. Everything else (the 503 body, `fleet_peer_guard`, the ban on calling `peer_only` directly, zero diff in `lan_cowork_fleet_security.rs`) is identical to F3c1.<br>**Concurrency is 1 job for the entire node** (not per peer). `active_jobs` is scanned in full without filtering by peer, and the check plus insertion happen in a single critical section. Get this wrong and **different peers could simultaneously git pull and self-replace**.<br>**The `local:` allowlist match is not input validation** —— it sits inside a detached task, and **even when disallowed, the HTTP response is 200 plus a `job_id`**. The rejection is observed via `/fleet/update/status` (already ported in F3a) as `status:"failed"` / `error:"local_path_not_allowed"` / `steps[0].output`. Rejecting synchronously with a 400 would break status-code parity, and the 409 job slot would also go unconsumed. An `Err` from `canonicalize()` is handled as: **the input side is rejected immediately, while the entry side is treated as a non-match and scanning continues** (aborting on the entry side would mean a single typo in an allowed path wipes out all `local:` updates).<br>**Failed jobs are also persisted to disk** —— the caller of `save_last_job` exists on the route side too, and runs regardless of success or failure. Saving only pre-restart would mean status returns 404 after a restart, breaking parity.<br>Restart reuses F3c1's seam, job persistence reuses F3a's `save_last_job`, and authorization reuses F2's `check_update_allowed`, **without rewriting any of them**.

### Fixed

- **Closed the problem where the fleet tests could launch real git** (present since F3a). Split `run_git` into a `#[cfg(not(test))]` production implementation and a `#[cfg(test)]` seam, **placing no fallback to real git in the seam** (an unconfigured or exhausted queue is an immediate error). Also folded F3a's `git_short_head` into the same path. This lets tests pin the **command sequence and order** of `git_precheck` → `fetch` → `pull --ff-only`.<br>Also fixed a **self-deadlock** caused by re-acquiring the same mutex while still holding the `MutexGuard` from `git_test_commands().lock()` (the same pattern as F2's consent test — with the same symptom too, since libtest doesn't report "exceeded 60 seconds," this was **misdiagnosed as real git's network wait**).

## [4.563.0] - 2026-08-05

### Added

- Fifth stage of the LAN Cowork fleet group port (F3c1). Ported `/fleet/restart` to Rust. **This increment is a destructive operation** (process self-replacement), so a mistake could **allow an arbitrary node to be restarted remotely**. The design required two design-advisor rulings (rev1 = NO-GO/9 must-fix items, rev2 = GO-with-conditions/3 must-fix items).<br>**Authorization reuses existing assets only** and introduces no new judgment —— 503 `{"ok": false, "error": "LAN Cowork not enabled"}` (**because `@auth_decorator` runs before the body's own `require_manager()`; distinct from F3b's `service_unavailable`**) → `fleet_peer_guard` (Python is keyed to the in-memory registry / Rust to the DB `peers` table, so calling `peer_only` directly yields Python=403 vs. Rust=200) → F2's already-ported `check_update_allowed(.., allow_consent=true, include_restart_allowlist=true)`. **Consent and the allowlist are mutually exclusive** (if `allow_remote_update=false`, only consent applies; if `true`, only the allowlist applies — they are not additive).<br>**Process self-replacement preserves the same per-OS branches as Python** —— Linux uses `libc::execv` (preserves the PID, hence systemd-compatible; under `Restart=on-failure`, exit 0 does not trigger a restart; and because `KillMode=control-group`, any spawned successor gets killed), macOS uses `Command` + `pre_exec(libc::setsid)`, Windows uses `Command` + `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`. **The argv construction differs per branch** —— execv uses `[current_exe, ..args_os().skip(1)]`, while spawn uses `Command::new(current_exe).args(args_os().skip(1))`. Writing `.args(args_os())` would duplicate `argv[0]`, and since `Cli` has only long options and no positional argument, clap would `exit(2)`, causing **the node to stop immediately after returning 200**. If `current_exe()` shows `" (deleted)"` (a Linux-procfs-specific marker), the operation is aborted. Uses `args_os()` (`args()` panics on non-UTF-8).<br>The restart seam is placed at the **"reservation"** point —— the `tokio::spawn` call itself is the seam, closing `sleep(1500ms)` and the exec inside it. Placing it after the `sleep` would make the check "the seam is not called on authorization failure" trivially true immediately after the response, losing discriminative power. The seam avoids an `FnOnce`-take type in favor of `AtomicUsize` (because that would make verifying double-acceptance structurally impossible; Python likewise doesn't restrict this, since it uses two daemon threads).

### Fixed

- **Fixed poor isolation in the fleet tests** (present since F3b; surfaced during F3c1's implementation). All fleet tests were reading and writing the **same `config.json`** directly under the working directory, so one test could see `allow_log_stream_from` written by another and pass authorization it shouldn't, letting the negative path proceed all the way to a **500**. Which test failed varied with execution order, and because it **passed when run alone**, this was not caught by F3b's landing-time verification (running once in the same order). ⟹ Isolated the test state's `config_path` into per-test `tempdir`s and made the consent guard module-shared. **Going forward, the standard is one serial run plus multiple parallel runs.**

## [4.562.0] - 2026-08-05

### Added

- Fourth stage of the LAN Cowork fleet group port (F3b). Ported `/fleet/logs/stream` (SSE plus relay) to Rust. **The hardest of the five fleet routes; the design required four design-advisor rulings** (rev1 through rev3 were NO-GO). **Authorization splits into three branches**, so F3a's single shared guard type cannot be reused —— relay (503 → **session 401** → chief 404 → unknown-peer 404) / peer (503 → registry-membership 403 → pubkey 403 → signature → nonce → Bearer → allowlist 403) / browser (503 → **session 401 only**). **Applying peer authentication to branch 3 breaks the browser path** (immediate 401 without `X-Peer-Id`), and **evaluating branch 2 first lets a remote peer walk into the relay**. On the SSE side there are four differences in the ported primitives —— `get_since` does not exist in Rust, so live uses broadcast; `recent` takes three arguments (Python takes two); **the seq origin is Rust=0 vs. Python=1**, so `after_seq=Some(0)` drops the very first entry; `level_rank` is `pub(super)` and cannot be called from routes (**only its visibility is widened to `pub(crate)`**; re-copying the rank logic is disallowed). **The core point is to call `subscribe()` before `recent()`** — in the reverse order, any log that arrives in the gap is **permanently lost, silently**（Python documents this same trap in a comment). Since neither function is async with an await point between them, a `#[cfg(test)]` seam was cut to pin the order in tests. The payload maps `target`→`source` and `WARN`→`WARNING` **only at serialization time** (rewriting `ring.rs` would break the native viewer and its regression tests). The `level` query **validates the exact match against the four allowed words first, then maps afterward** (doing it in the reverse order would silently disable the filter). `RecvError::Lagged` **neither disconnects nor emits `tracing::warn!`** (a warn would be re-injected into the ring, creating a possible lag→warn→lag feedback loop). **A pre-connection failure on the relay emits only `event: close`**, never `event: error` —— Python catches with `except Exception`, swallows it, and sends only close in `finally` (`event: error` is reserved for the case of "reached the peer but got a non-200"). Review flagged that "there is not a single test on this path," so a test asserting the **absence** of `event: error` was added. Discriminative power was **demonstrated by automating five mutations** (guard always-fails → 8 positive-path tests fail, session always-fails → 4 fail, reversing the `subscribe`/`recent` order → the seam test fails).

## [4.561.3] - 2026-08-04

### Fixed

- **Fixed a problem where `/ext/lan_cowork/fleet/logs/stream` could serve full log contents without authentication** (Python side). Discovered during investigation for the F3b port. **Anyone on the LAN, without authentication or pairing, could continuously view the full logs over SSE simply by sending `X-Peer-Id: <the target node's own peer_id>`.** The path to exploitation had four steps: (1) `bypass_session=True` makes `auth_chain_checks.py:45-47` return `AuthResult(passed=True, reason=declared.require)`, letting it slip past the session gate (**`require` is nothing more than a reason string**); (2) **this is the only one of the fleet's 5 routes without an `@auth_decorator`**, so none of signature, nonce, or Bearer is checked; (3) `X-Peer-Id` is trusted without verification; (4) `check_log_stream_allowed`'s `requester_peer_id == local_peer_id → True` unconditionally bypasses the allowlist (`local_peer_id` can be obtained with a single unauthenticated call to `/ext/lan_cowork/api/peer/status`). **Not even QuickLock defends against this** —— `auth_chain_runner.py:18`'s `_STATIC_CHECKS` runs before `check_quick_lock`, so **the more a configuration relies on a PIN, the more it is betrayed**. And LAN Cowork is **enabled by default** (`extension.json`'s `config.enabled: true`; `extensions_loader_manifest.py:174`'s `get("enabled", True)`). What is exposed is the very **same ring buffer's full, continuous log view** that `routes/logs_api.py:101` protects with `_require_admin_scope()`. ⟹ Extracted the body of `require_peer_auth` into `authenticate_peer_request()` (without duplicating the cryptographic verification), and applied it **only to the peer branch**. Unconditionally attaching `@auth_decorator` was ruled out because it would cause an immediate 401 without `X-Peer-Id`, breaking both the browser path and the relay path. Removed the self-declared allowlist bypass (also removing the now-unnecessary `local_peer_id` argument). **Since relay origins already attach signature, nonce, and Bearer** (`fleet_peer_http.py:14-45`), the only gap was the receiver's failure to verify them, so **the legitimate path is unchanged**.

- **Resolved the risk of CMA exhaustion from owner collisions in `acquire_device`** (Python side). Discovered as a side effect of the Hailo boundary review. `acquire_device(owner, hef_path)`'s owner string is a **globally coordinated namespace**, but `"yolo"` was shared between `builtin_hailo_yolo_detect` (selectable by the user via settings) and LAN Cowork's `yolo_engine.py` (fixed order, first-come). If the model is set to `yolov11n` while `yolov8n.hef` is also present, this becomes **the same owner with a different HEF**, and the two mutually evict each other via the "Model switch" path. Since LAN Cowork re-acquires on every inference (without releasing), this causes not only second-level HEF-load thrashing but also leaves behind the DMA mappings `backend_hailo.py:35-43` reserved in advance. **`device_manager_infer.py:57-63` explicitly documents CMA exhaustion as an irreversible failure requiring "a full system restart."** ⟹ Renamed only the LAN Cowork side's owner to `"lan-yolo"` (2 files, 2 lines). The `builtin_hailo_yolo_detect` side was left unchanged to preserve the existing UI display. `"clip"` is likewise shared, but with the current call pattern it uses the same HEF, so a Model switch does not occur (though `get_encoder(hef_dir)` can point at a different directory, so "always identical" does not hold strictly). Noted in the test that **CMA exhaustion itself cannot be pinned by a test since it requires real hardware**.

## [4.561.2] - 2026-08-01

### Fixed

- Aggregated LAN Cowork inbound SSE's dropped-event logging for absent recipients into 60-second buckets, logging the first occurrence immediately, to prevent excessive log output.

### Changed

- Updated agent workflow and environment metadata to match current operations.

## [4.561.1] - 2026-08-01

### Fixed

- Fixed the Codex Security scan's supply-chain, update, LAN, UI, archive, and Tauri boundaries. Pinned release Actions and portable download/dependencies to immutable identifiers and SHA-256 hash locks, tied the payload of an unsigned ZIP that the reviewer reads in a single pass to the reviewed path and forbidden policy, protected LAN import with a one-shot session, a persistent-extraction-volume quota, and ZIP-bomb limits, and restricted the isolated Extension DB RPC with dynamic capabilities, SQLite execution-volume limits, and reverse-peer PID/nonce checks.

## [4.561.0] - 2026-08-01

### Added

- Third stage (F3a) of the LAN Cowork fleet-group port. Ported the 2 routes `/fleet/info` and `/fleet/update/status` to Rust. **The design received a design-advisor ruling twice; rev1 was NO-GO (9 must-fixes)** — because it overlooked the `@auth_decorator` (`fleet_routes_update_job.py:137`) on `/fleet/update/status` and wrongly concluded that "no authentication is enforced at all", and because the design document had **instructed removal of the authentication**. In fact both routes pass through the same decorator bound to `require_peer_auth` at `fleet_routes.py:84,97,110,144`, enforcing X-Peer-Id → registry membership (403) → pubkey → Ed25519 signature → **single-use nonce** → Bearer token. ⟹ The implementation was structured so both routes pass through a shared `fleet_peer_guard`, so authorization cannot diverge. When LAN Cowork is disabled (`peer_registry` unconfigured), it returns **503 before auth** (same ordering as `peer_auth.py:92-95`). Auto-heal uses `git rev-parse --short HEAD` (without `--short` it compares a 40-character hash against a shortened one and **silently, permanently never fires**). The `status` value is **lowercase**, same as Python. The job-record lookup is two-staged: ① the in-memory `active_jobs` is returned **without healing**, and ② only the disk path heals. Only **2 exact paths** were added to `check_static_bypass` (a prefix is forbidden because it would expose `/fleet/update`).

## [4.560.0] - 2026-08-01

### Added

- Second stage (F2) of the LAN Cowork fleet-group port. Ported **9 peer-facing routes + the authorization mechanism** to Rust — 6 consent routes (`request`/`respond`/`status/<id>`/`pending`/`relay/request`/`relay/status`), 3 allowlists routes (`grant`/`revoke`/`check`), plus the 4-way authorization branching covering consent-token single-use, the 60-second periodic janitor, and `fleet_route_security`. Because **`@auth_route(require=...)` is declarative metadata and enforces nothing at runtime** (`core/web/auth_route_policy.py` only registers it), enforcement is held individually by each route body. To match Python's measured behavior, this was **split by type** into 3 guards — `session_only` / `peer_only` / `session_and_chief` (a form that cannot be unioned). The allowlist categories are the same 2 as Python: `log_stream` and `update`. `status()` detects undecided and expired entries at read time and deletes them, returning `"expired"` (it does not wait for the janitor). `pending()` carries the same expiry conjunction. `require_peer_auth_with_nonce_store` was extracted, but **the production path still passes `nonce_store()` as before**, so behavior is unchanged (it is a seam for tests to inject a store with grace 0).

## [4.558.0] - 2026-07-31

### Fixed

- **Fixed an issue where a large-library LAN Cowork full import would show "completed" while ending with 0 items** (both Rust and Python sides). Because the ids for the bulk zip fetch were placed on a single URL without splitting, at around 6,500–9,500 items (depending on id digit width) hyper's request-target limit of 65,534 bytes was exceeded, producing a 414; and because `download_zip` returned an empty map on any non-200 response, no degradation occurred either, and `completed` was recorded regardless. Ids are now split into batches of 500. Since this is larger than `BATCH_THRESHOLD` (100), the normal case of 100–499 items still makes 1 request as before. Degradation to individual HTTP requests when the zip size limit fires is now scoped to that chunk only.

## [4.557.0] - 2026-07-31

### Added

- Added an upper limit on the number of bytes received by LAN Cowork import (both Rust and Python sides). `download_file` is 8 GiB, `download_zip` is 2 GiB. The check happens before writing, using only absolute values, never peer-supplied numbers. When the zip limit fires it degrades to individual HTTP requests rather than failing, so import does not stop.

## [4.549.0] - 2026-07-29

### Added

- **Ported the helpers of the LAN Cowork import transfer layer to Rust (Increment L3b-1)**: gathered `unique_dest` / `validate_zip_entry_name` / `verify_within` into `routes/lan_cowork_import_transfer.rs`. The route has not been grown yet and lands as dead code. **This is the core of the zip-slip countermeasure** — the reason R2b (v4.544.0) decided not to sanitize `arcname` on the sending side was that "the receiving side guards doubly," and this increment is that receiving side. **`verify_within` compares only after resolving** — `path_guard::path_is_within` only **strips the `\\?\` prefix as a string** and never calls `canonicalize`; it is a predicate for "comparison," not "normalization" (both of its existing 2 call sites pass already-canonicalized values). Writing with that predicate alone would let both an outward-pointing symlink and a bare `..` pass straight through, effectively disabling traversal protection. Therefore `resolve_non_strict` (sequential realpath) from S1 was made `pub(crate)` and reused, resolving both sides before comparing. `validate_zip_entry_name` normalizes `\` → `/` **before all other checks** (the `12/..\..\x.txt` case raised in R2b is caught by `..` detection here). Rejection reasons are returned as an enum, and the entry name itself is not logged. `unique_dest` matches Python's behavior where the rename destination is `folder` (not `dest.parent`), and where **`Path.stem`/`suffix` handle a trailing dot specially** (measured: `Path("a.").stem == "a."` / `.suffix == ""`). 5 tests. Design: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-lan-cowork-import-transfer-l3b1.md`

## [4.548.0] - 2026-07-29

### Added

- **Ported the LAN Cowork import DB persistence layer to Rust (Increment L3a)**: gathered `insert_file`/`write_metadata`/`persist_downloaded_file` of `import_executor_db.py` (181 lines) into `routes/lan_cowork_import_persist.rs`. The route has not been grown yet and lands as dead code. **The blast radius is effectively 10 tables** — in addition to the 6 tables written directly (`files`・`tags`・`file_tags`・`file_ratings`・`file_annotations`・`favorites`), the `files` INSERT updates `search_stats` and the **FTS5 index** via triggers, and the `file_tags` INSERT updates `search_stats` and `file_tag_counts` via triggers. Accordingly, the test DDL is copied from the production schema **including constraints and triggers** (reusing the existing read-only DDL would let `CHECK(rating)`・`value BLOB NOT NULL`・`path UNIQUE` all slip through unchecked, and without seeding `collections` id=1, verification of the Favorites-skip case would pass only by an AUTOINCREMENT coincidence). `insert_file` **never uses `last_insert_rowid()`**, always looking up by path instead (to avoid the same bug that v4.547.1 fixed on the Python side). The callback for `resolve_collection_id` would be a double borrow in Rust and is **impossible to implement**, so it was settled as a direct call instead. Decoding of the annotation value is **the receiving side of R1's encoding** (this is why R1 was not allowed to decompress zstd — the receiving side decodes base64 and INSERTs it verbatim). Because **`dict.get(k, default)` returns the default only when the key is absent**, `null` is not silently absorbed but distinguished from it. Also implemented re-wrapping for the case where `ann_rows` is a string (dropping it would silently lose annotation data). 51 tests. Design: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-lan-cowork-import-persist-l3a.md`

## [4.547.1] - 2026-07-29

### Fixed

- **Import metadata could be written to the wrong file (data corruption)**: `insert_file` in `import_executor_db.py` trusted `cur.lastrowid` after an `INSERT OR IGNORE`. **When the INSERT is ignored, `lastrowid` is neither `None` nor 0 — it returns the id of the last successful INSERT on the same connection** (measured: on Python 3.13.13 / SQLite 3.50.4, re-inserting the row with id 1 gave `lastrowid = 2`). ⇒ `insert_file` returned the wrong file id, and since `persist_downloaded_file` calls `write_metadata` with that id, **tags, ratings, annotations, and collections could be written to a different file**. Because batch import uses a shared write connection, this fires **from the second file onward whose destination path collides with an existing row** (`ImportPlanner` skips by hash, but a file with no hash always lands in `to_import`). The first item falls back to the existing SELECT fallback and returns the correct id, which is **why only the second item onward broke, making this hard to notice**. Stopped relying on `lastrowid` and now always looks it up via `SELECT id FROM files WHERE path=?` (the same SELECT already existed, but the `if cur.lastrowid:` branch never let it be reached). Discovered and confirmed by measurement while starting the LAN Cowork Rust port (L3a). Added a regression test (confirmed it fails with `assert 2 == 1` before the fix).

## [4.547.0] - 2026-07-29

### Added

- **Ported the write side of the LAN Cowork import ledger to Rust (Increment L2b)**: gathered `create`/`update`/`register_file`/`get_or_create_collection`. The route has not been grown yet and lands as dead code. **Transaction discipline is the central topic** — the API is unified on `&mut SqliteConnection` (`Executor` is consumed by value, so a function issuing 2+ statements cannot be written generically over it; `impl Acquire` also defeats the purpose of a shared transaction when given `&SqlitePool`, since it takes a separate connection each time), core issues no `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`, and the wrapper does `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` plus **ROLLBACK on every error path** (including when `COMMIT` itself fails — dropping this would return the connection to the pool mid-transaction, breaking everything else on that connection afterward). **The 2 statements of `register_file` must sit in the same transaction** — calling it on a bare connection would split them under autocommit, committing only the INSERT into the map while the increment to `done_files` is lost, permanently under-reporting progress. `get_or_create_collection` INSERTs into the core table `collections`, performing `LOWER(TRIM(name))` matching **on the SQL side** (`'école'` and `'ÉCOLE'` are different collections), **logs only the count on multiple matches, never the names** (because they come from a peer; Python does print the names), and **makes the choice among ambiguous matches deterministic** via `ORDER BY id` (Python's `existing[0][0]` has no ORDER BY and is genuinely non-deterministic). `update` allowlists 5 columns (not including `options`), silently discards anything outside the allowlist, and **because of the dirty check, the UPDATE itself is never issued and `updated_at` does not move either**. 43 tests. Design: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-lan-cowork-import-state-l2b.md`

## [4.546.0] - 2026-07-29

### Added

- **Ported the LAN Cowork import planning layer and ledger read side to Rust (Increment L2a)**: gathered `ImportPlanner.plan` and `ImportSession`'s `get`/`list_all`/`is_file_processed`/`get_local_file_id` into `routes/lan_cowork_import_state.rs`. The write side (`create`/`update`/`register_file`/`get_or_create_collection`) was split off into **L2b** — because the estimate of roughly 945 lines exceeded the self-imposed cap, and because the points of contention concentrate on the write side. The route has not been grown yet and lands as dead code. The 3 DB tables were already defined, but **had zero references from the Rust side**. **Every function returns `Result`** (swallowing errors would make `plan` return everything as `to_import` and re-download the entire library). **A missing peer-supplied `id` fails closed** (the initial implementation used `unwrap_or(Value::Null)`, fail-open, silently letting `null` in on bad peer data; Python raises `KeyError` on `f["id"]`). R1's chunk/dedup helper was made generic **only over its type parameter** and reused, sharing `IN_CHUNK_SIZE` as well. `options` is parsed and returned, and a parse failure is also an `Err`. The test DDL is copied column-by-column from the production schema. 38 tests (including R1's 25). Design: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-lan-cowork-import-state-l2.md`

## [4.545.0] - 2026-07-29

### Added

- **Ported LAN Cowork's signed outbound peer transport to Rust (Increment L1)**: gathered the wiring corresponding to Python's `PeerTransport` (`core_impl/transport.py`, 169 lines) into `routes/lan_cowork_transport.rs` (the signing primitives and outbound foundation already existed, but `make_signature_headers` had zero production callers). Since all 5 local_import routes are outbound clients, this transport now becomes the prerequisite for all of them. The route has not been grown yet and lands as dead code. **The direction of 401 token invalidation must not be gotten backwards** — `revoke_token` revokes `peer_tokens.revoked_at` (the **inbound token this side issued to the peer**), so misusing it would make incoming requests from the peer return 401, and `renew_if_not_revoked` would also refuse reissuance, so **it would not recover until re-pairing**. The correct target is only the 3 token columns of `peers` via `PeerRegistry::upsert` (the **outbound credentials this side presents to the peer**). **The signing invariant is "send exactly the byte string that was signed"** — `json.dumps` and `serde_json` disagree on key order, non-ASCII representation, and floats, but since the signature target is the byte string this side itself sends, wire compatibility is unaffected. `reqwest`'s `.json()` re-serializes, so it is forbidden; `.body(bytes)` is used instead. Also implemented: a seam for injecting the timestamp (also pinning the nonce branch through the same function), overwriting `X-Requested-With: PeerTransport`, a parameterized response-body cap (default 64 MiB for JSON fetches — the existing 64 KiB would always be hit by `/import/meta?mode=full`), a 5-second timeout, a guard that the signed path/query matches the actual URL, and 2 events on 401. **The response body is not logged** (Python writes it wholesale at WARN level, but since it is a known leak path this was not replicated). 8 tests. Design: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-lan-cowork-outbound-transport-l1.md`

## [4.544.1] - 2026-07-28

### Fixed

- **`register-path` accepted paths outside the scan root and disallowed extensions**: Rust's `register_path` was **missing two** of the checks that Python's `register_path_payload` (`services_drop_upload.py:234-277`) has, letting admin scope alone **register any existing path into `files`** (no scan-root containment, no extension allowlist, no `is_file()` check). Since v4.544.0's remote import R2b introduced **a surface that delivers the file body of a path listed in the DB to a peer**, this created a chain that **did not exist in Python**: "an admin registers an arbitrary file → a paired peer retrieves it" (R2b's deny-list only covers system areas, so a user's private files such as `~/Documents/*.pdf` pass straight through). This restores the **origin** of the chain to the same strength as Python. Tightening the acceptance conditions breaks no path (the UI's rescan **already fails with 409** due to the UNIQUE constraint on `files.path`, and the MCP and user-facing docs already require paths inside the scan root). Configuration is read via **`read_config_json` on every request**, not from `app_config` (a startup snapshot) — getting this wrong would produce an undiagnosable stall where "`register-path` alone rejects everything even though the root exists in the UI." The comparison predicate is also consolidated into `crates/yu-server/src/path_guard.rs` and used by both R2b's deny-list and this increment's allow-list (sharing only the normalizer would mean **Windows users couldn't register even inside the scan root** — because case-folding lived on the caller's side). The value that gets INSERTed is left unchanged (normalizing it would turn a 200 into a 409). A permanent rule is added to the `windows:` section of `arch-constraints.yaml`. Tests: `tools_ops` 27 / `path_guard` 2 / `lan_cowork_import` 25. Design: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-register-path-scan-root-guard.md`

## [4.544.0] - 2026-07-28

### Added

- **Port LAN Cowork remote import's file-delivery surface to Rust (Increment R2b)**: Adds `/file/{id}`, `/zip`, and `/stream/{id}`, completing `remote_import_api.py` (291 lines) entirely on the Rust side. **The decisive difference from R2a is the new surface that delivers the file body itself** (R2a delivered only the basename and did not follow symlinks). Since `main.rs:3189` has no proxy fallback, these previously returned 404. **A read-side deny-list is introduced in this increment** — the write side already had a deny-list, but the read side had no counterpart. An allow-list (inside the scan root) couldn't be used because scan roots are mutable config and `files` rows outlive them; a deny-list, on the other hand, can be added **without changing the response schema by even one line**, and also covers symlink paths. Watch out for the **Windows verbatim prefix (`\\?\`) trap** — canonicalizing only one side and then using `starts_with` never matches on Windows, silently disabling the entire deny-list (this doesn't happen on POSIX, so Linux development wouldn't notice it). **The conclusion depends on polarity**: an allow-list form is fail-closed, while a deny-list form is **fail-open**. The full inventory is in `docs/development/development_docs/WINDOWS_VERBATIM_PATH_PITFALL.md`. Also: registered 3 routes into `check_static_bypass` (a broad prefix like `/import/` is forbidden), moved the Semaphore permit into the closure via `acquire_owned()` (`spawn_blocking` cannot be cancelled), split the parsing rules for `{file_id}` (unsigned, 404) and `ids` (`i64`, `-1` is 404 `no files`), used `is_file()` (`exists()` **hangs forever on a FIFO**), always sets `large_file(true)` for ZIP, does not sanitize `arcname`, and propagates entry-read failures (500). Tests: 25 + `auth::chain` 30. Design: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-lan-cowork-remote-import-r2b-files.md`

## [4.543.1] - 2026-07-28

### Fixed

- **remote import's `meta`/`diff` sat inside the session gate, unreachable by peers**: `auth/chain.rs`'s `check_static_bypass` **enumerates LAN Cowork's peer routes one by one as exact paths** (L144 in the same file explicitly states "exact paths, never a prefix"), but forgot to add the 2 routes created by R2a (v4.543.0). On the Python side, `auth_route(..., bypass_session=True, require="peer")` grants the bypass **declaratively**, so the omission arose from the Rust side's hand-written enumeration. R2a's tests run the Router directly with oneshot, so they **don't go through the middleware** and didn't catch this. Along with the fix, a regression test that calls `check_static_bypass` directly was added, pinning both the 2 permitted routes and the fact that **`local_import_api`'s 5 session-based routes are not bypassed** (to prevent this from recurring as a prefix — since routes sharing session auth share the same prefix). With `native_daemon` off by default, **production impact is currently zero**, and the failure direction was fail-closed (401) too, but since shipped code doesn't function, this is fixed on its own ahead of R2b.

## [4.543.0] - 2026-07-28

### Added

- **Serve LAN Cowork remote import's `meta`/`diff` from Rust (Increment R2a)**: Adds an HTTP surface on top of R1's DB-query/formatting layer, creating the 2 routes `/api/peer/import/meta` and `/diff`. `file`/`zip`/`stream` are split off to **R2b** — the decisive difference from R1 is that this "**creates a surface that did not previously exist on the Rust node**" (there is no proxy fallback at `main.rs:3189`, so it currently returns 404), and increments that involve file delivery are reviewed separately.
